punnett.title: Punnett Square
punnett.description: Here you enter the genotype of each parent for one gene. The table shows which allele pairs the offspring can receive, and the ratio panel shows their genotypes and phenotypes.
punnett.alleleHint: Use a capital letter for the dominant allele, for example B, and a lower-case letter for the recessive allele, for example b. Try BB × bb, Bb × Bb or AA × aa.
punnett.invalidHint: Both parents need two alleles of the same gene, for example Bb × bb. Do not mix letters for different genes, such as A and B, in one cross.

contrast.en: The genotype ratio (1 : 2 : 1) and the phenotype ratio (3 : 1, dominant : recessive) are not the same: for Bb × Bb, BB and Bb show the same phenotype.
contrast.ru: Соотношение генотипов (1 : 2 : 1) и соотношение фенотипов (3 : 1, доминантный : рецессивный) — не одно и то же: при Bb × Bb генотипы BB и Bb имеют одинаковый фенотип.

model.en: Each cell is one possible genotype for one child, and the four cells are equally likely. To find a chance, count the cells with the genotype or phenotype you need and divide by four. For Bb × bb, two of the four cells are Bb, so the chance of Bb is 2/4, or 50 per cent. The grid gives a chance for each child, not a guaranteed group of four children.
model.ru: Каждая клетка — один возможный генотип потомка, и все четыре клетки равновероятны. Чтобы найти вероятность, посчитай клетки с нужным генотипом или фенотипом и раздели на четыре. Например, при Bb × bb две из четырёх клеток имеют генотип Bb, значит, вероятность Bb равна 2/4 (50 %). Решётка показывает вероятность для каждого потомка, а не гарантированный набор из четырёх детей.

cellDiagram.title: Animal and plant cell diagram
cellDiagram.description: Compare a typical animal cell with a photosynthetic plant cell. The diagram is simplified: it omits many components, and specialised cells can look different.
cellDiagram.plantExtras: The photosynthetic plant cell in this diagram has three extra parts: a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole.
cellDiagram.hoverHint: Tap or hover a part to see its function.

nucleus.label: Nucleus
nucleus.desc: Contains most of the cell’s DNA. Nuclear pores control exchange with the cytoplasm; mRNA leaves the nucleus through them.

nucleolus.label: Nucleolus
nucleolus.desc: Nuclear region where ribosomal RNA is made and ribosomal subunits are assembled.

mitochondria.label: Mitochondria
mitochondria.desc: Most stages of aerobic respiration take place here. The energy released is stored in ATP.

ribosome.label: Ribosomes
ribosome.desc: Ribosomes join amino acids to make proteins, using instructions carried by mRNA. They have no surrounding membrane.

membrane.label: Cell membrane
membrane.desc: Controls which substances enter and leave the cell. It is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins in it.

cytoplasm.label: Cytoplasm
cytoplasm.desc: The material inside the cell membrane, excluding the nucleus. It includes fluid and organelles; many chemical reactions happen here.

wall.label: Cell wall
wall.desc: Rigid layer outside the cell membrane. It stops the cell from bursting when water enters.

chloroplast.label: Chloroplast
chloroplast.desc: Site of photosynthesis. Chlorophyll in the thylakoid membranes absorbs light.

vacuole.label: Vacuole
vacuole.desc: Large sac filled with cell sap. It stores water and dissolved substances and keeps the cell firm.

contrast.en: The cell wall lies outside the cell membrane and does not replace it. Plant cells have both.
contrast.ru: Клеточная стенка лежит снаружи клеточной мембраны и не заменяет её. У растительных клеток есть и стенка, и мембрана.

heartDiagram.title: Heart Diagram
heartDiagram.description: Follow the pulmonary and systemic circulation through the four chambers. Colours show relative oxygen content.
heartDiagram.hoverHint: Choose a chamber or vessel by clicking, tapping, or using Tab and Enter/Space to read its function.
heartDiagram.doubleCirc: Double circulation: blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit of the body, first to the lungs and then to the rest of the body.

ra.label: Right atrium
ra.desc: Receives deoxygenated blood and passes it into the right ventricle.

rv.label: Right ventricle
rv.desc: Pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary artery.

la.label: Left atrium
la.desc: Receives oxygenated blood and passes it into the left ventricle.

lv.label: Left ventricle
lv.desc: Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta. Its wall is the thickest of the four chambers.

vc.label: Vena cava
vc.desc: The superior and inferior venae cavae carry deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium.

pa.label: Pulmonary artery
pa.desc: Carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.

pv.label: Pulmonary vein
pv.desc: Carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

ao.label: Aorta
ao.desc: The largest artery. It carries oxygenated blood to the organs and tissues of the body.

contrast.en: Left and right mean the person's own sides, not the viewer's. On this diagram the left side (LA, LV, PV, AO) is drawn on the right of the picture.
contrast.ru: Левое и правое — это стороны самого человека, а не зрителя. На схеме левая сторона (LA, LV, PV, AO) нарисована справа.

photoDepth.title: Photosynthesis — extension
photoDepth.body: In chloroplasts, the light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes. They use light energy to make ATP and NADPH, and they split water, releasing oxygen. The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma. It uses ATP and NADPH to fix CO₂ into 3-carbon molecules. The Calvin cycle does not use light directly, but it slows down when the light-dependent reactions stop.

contrast.en: Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials. Light supplies energy, not matter. Plants also respire in both light and darkness.
contrast.ru: Углекислый газ и вода — сырьё фотосинтеза. Свет даёт энергию, а не вещество. Растения дышат и на свету, и в темноте.

hormones.title: Hormones in depth
items: Insulin from pancreatic beta cells promotes glucose uptake into cells and its storage as glycogen, which lowers blood glucose.
Glucagon from pancreatic alpha cells promotes liver glucose production and release.
Adrenaline, produced by the adrenal glands, prepares the body for fast action: the heart beats faster and the liver releases glucose into the blood.

Oestrogens and testosterone are present in both males and females, but in different amounts. Testosterone is usually higher in males, and oestrogens are usually higher in females. Both hormones affect reproductive development and other functions.
Thyroid hormones, such as thyroxine, increase the metabolic rate in most body tissues, so the body uses more energy.

contrast.en: A hormone is carried in the blood to all tissues, but only target cells with the right receptors respond to it.
contrast.ru: Гормон переносится кровью ко всем тканям, но отвечают на него только клетки-мишени с нужными рецепторами.

genetics.title: Genetics — mutations and codons
genetics.body: An mRNA codon is a three-nucleotide sequence specifying an amino acid or a stop signal. AUG usually initiates translation and specifies methionine. Mutations change DNA: insertions or deletions shift a coding reading frame only when their length is not a multiple of three.

contrast.en: Genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism. Phenotype is the set of observable characteristics, influenced by genotype and environment.
contrast.ru: Генотип (genotype) — генетический состав организма. Фенотип (phenotype) — совокупность наблюдаемых признаков, на которые влияют генотип и среда.

biotech.title: Biotechnology
items: Selective breeding means choosing parents with desired heritable traits, so that those traits become more common in later generations.
In genetic engineering, DNA is changed directly, either within one species or by moving a gene between species.
Cloning produces genetically identical copies, but mutations and the environment can still cause differences between them.
CRISPR-based editing changes selected DNA sequences precisely, but scientists must check for unwanted changes at other sites.
Ethical assessment checks evidence of safety, consent, the welfare of organisms, effects on the environment and access to the technology.

contrast.en: Genetic engineering is one part of biotechnology, not all of it. Making yoghurt with bacterial cultures is also biotechnology, even though no gene is moved between species.
contrast.ru: Генная инженерия — только одна часть биотехнологии. Приготовление йогурта на бактериальных культурах тоже относится к биотехнологии, хотя ни один ген не переносится между видами.

homeostasis.title: Homeostasis
homeostasis.body: Homeostasis is the maintenance of internal conditions within ranges compatible with cell function, despite changes inside and outside the body. Negative feedback reduces a deviation from the set value. Conditions fluctuate around regulated values rather than staying perfectly constant.

contrast.en: Homeostasis is the goal of regulation, not a mechanism. Hormones and the nervous system are two tools that keep it.
contrast.ru: Гомеостаз — цель регуляции, а не механизм. Гормоны и нервная система — два средства, которыми его поддерживают.

cells.title: Cell Biology
cells.intro: All living organisms are made of cells, the basic unit of life. Animal and plant cells share many structures but differ from each other, and specialised cells are adapted to their functions.

light.name: Light microscope
light.rule: A light microscope forms a magnified image using visible light and lenses. Magnification is image size ÷ actual size. Resolution is the smallest distance between two points at which they can still be seen as separate. A conventional light microscope has a resolution of about 0.2 μm. If two points are not resolved, enlarging the image adds no detail.
examples: Eyepiece ×10 multiplied by objective ×40 gives total magnification ×400.
With a light microscope you can see whole plant and animal cells, nuclei, chloroplasts and vacuoles. In a living sample you can also see the cytoplasm moving.
A conventional light microscope cannot resolve ribosomes, mitochondrial internal detail or the thickness of the lipid bilayer.
Two points 0.1 μm apart merge into one blurred spot in a light microscope, because its resolution is about 0.2 μm.
light.tip: The smaller the resolution limit, the finer the detail you can see. A microscope with a limit of 0.2 μm shows more detail than one with a limit of 1 μm.

contrast.en: Magnification is a ratio with no unit, such as ×400. Resolution is a distance, such as 0.2 μm.
contrast.ru: Увеличение — безразмерная величина, например ×400. Предел разрешения — расстояние, например 0,2 мкм.

electron.name: Electron microscope
electron.rule: An electron microscope forms an image using a beam of electrons and electromagnetic lenses. Its resolving power is much higher than that of a light microscope. A transmission electron microscope (TEM) shows the internal structure of thin specimens, while a scanning electron microscope (SEM) shows surface detail. Conventional preparation and the vacuum inside the microscope prevent observation of living cells.
examples: A TEM image of a thin section shows the internal membranes of a mitochondrion.
A SEM image shows the surface shape of a pollen grain.
electron.watchOut: Resolution depends on instrument and specimen preparation; there is no single maximum magnification for all electron microscopes.

contrast.en: Electron micrographs are black and white. Colour is added later and does not show the true colour of the specimen.
contrast.ru: Электронные микрофотографии чёрно-белые. Цвет на них добавляют позже, и он не показывает настоящий цвет образца.

preparation.name: Preparing a wet mount
preparation.rule: A wet mount holds a thin specimen in liquid between a slide and coverslip. Lower the coverslip at an angle to reduce bubbles, then locate and focus the specimen with the lowest-magnification objective. A suitable stain increases contrast but may kill cells or alter structures.
examples: A thin layer of onion epidermis is placed in a drop of water and covered with a coverslip.
Iodine solution is a common stain for onion cells. It colours the nucleus, so the nucleus is easier to see.
preparation.tip: Lower the objective slowly while watching from the side, so that the lens does not hit the coverslip.

contrast.en: A wet mount is only for light microscopes. Electron microscope samples are fixed and placed in a vacuum, and TEM samples are also cut into ultrathin sections.
contrast.ru: Временный препарат годится только для светового микроскопа. Образцы для электронного микроскопа фиксируют и помещают в вакуум, а образцы для TEM, кроме того, режут на ультратонкие срезы.

drawing.name: Biological drawings
drawing.rule: A biological drawing shows only the structures that you actually observed, with clear outlines, labels and a title. Include a scale bar or the magnification of the drawing. When you calculate magnification, use image size and actual size in the same units. If the drawing is resized, its magnification changes, so the microscope setting no longer applies to it.
examples: A drawing of one onion epidermal cell has the cell wall, cytoplasm, nucleus and vacuole labelled.
A cell 75 μm long seen at ×400 is 30 mm long on the drawing: 75 μm × 400 = 30 000 μm = 30 mm.
A structure 4 cm long on a drawing made at ×200 has a real length of 4 cm ÷ 200 = 0.02 cm, or 200 μm.
drawing.watchOut: Draw with a sharp pencil and single clean lines, without shading or colour. Do not add details that the microscope did not resolve.
drawing.tip: A scale bar stays correct when you resize the drawing, because the bar is resized with the image.

contrast.en: Image size is measured on the drawing or micrograph; actual size is the real size of the structure. Never substitute one for the other.
contrast.ru: Размер изображения измеряют на рисунке или микрофотографии, а реальный размер — это размер самого объекта. Их нельзя подменять друг другом.

eukaryotic.name: Eukaryotic cells
eukaryotic.rule:
Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus surrounded by a membrane and other membrane-bound organelles, such as mitochondria. Eukaryotes are animals, plants, fungi and protists, and all of them are made of these cells.

The nuclear envelope separates the DNA from the cytoplasm. The DNA in the nucleus is packed into linear chromosomes. Membrane-bound organelles divide the cell into compartments, so different reactions can run at the same time. Some specialised cells lose their nucleus as they mature, for example mammalian red blood cells.
examples: An onion bulb cell has a nucleus and mitochondria but no chloroplasts, and it is still eukaryotic.
A human body cell has 46 linear chromosomes in its nucleus, arranged in 23 pairs.
eukaryotic.tip: On a diagram or electron micrograph, look for a nucleus with a double membrane (the nuclear envelope). Its presence shows that the cell is eukaryotic.

contrast.en: A eukaryotic cell is not necessarily a plant cell. Animal cells are eukaryotic too, although they have no cell wall or chloroplasts.
contrast.ru: Эукариотическая клетка — не обязательно растительная. Животные клетки тоже эукариотические, хотя у них нет клеточной стенки и хлоропластов.

prokaryotic.name: Prokaryotic cells (bacteria)
prokaryotic.rule:
Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus surrounded by a membrane. Prokaryotes are bacteria and archaea.

Usually the chromosome is a single circular DNA molecule. It lies in a region called the nucleoid, which has no membrane around it. Many bacteria also carry small circular DNA molecules called plasmids. Prokaryotic cells have a cell membrane, cytoplasm and ribosomes. Most bacteria have a cell wall made of peptidoglycan, but archaeal walls are made of different molecules.
examples: E. coli is about 2 μm long and has one circular chromosome in its nucleoid.
Lactobacillus bacteria in yoghurt turn lactose into lactic acid, which makes the milk thicken.
prokaryotic.watchOut: A plasmid is not the main chromosome. It is a small ring of DNA that carries extra genes, for example genes that help the bacterium survive antibiotics. The bacterium can usually survive without it.

contrast.en: A nucleoid is not a nucleus. It holds the DNA but has no membrane around it.
contrast.ru: Нуклеоид — не ядро. В нём лежит ДНК, но его не окружает мембрана.

comparison.name: Comparing eukaryotes and prokaryotes
comparison.rule:
Compare the two cell types by these features.

Nucleus: eukaryotes have a nucleus surrounded by a membrane. Prokaryotes have no nucleus: their DNA lies in a nucleoid.

Chromosomes: eukaryotes usually have several linear chromosomes. Prokaryotes usually have one circular chromosome.

Membrane-bound organelles: eukaryotes have them, such as mitochondria. Prokaryotes do not.

Size: eukaryotic cells are usually 10–100 μm. Prokaryotic cells are usually 0.1–5 μm.

Cell wall: plants, fungi and most bacteria have one. Animal cells do not.
examples: A yeast cell, 5–10 μm across, is eukaryotic because it has a nucleus and mitochondria.
Ribosomes occur in both cell types and are not membrane-bound.
comparison.tip: In a comparison answer, name one feature and give both cell types in one sentence, for example: 'Eukaryotes have a nucleus with a membrane; prokaryotes have a nucleoid with no membrane.'

contrast.en: Viruses are not prokaryotes. They are not made of cells and have no ribosomes or cytoplasm of their own.
contrast.ru: Вирусы — не прокариоты. Они не состоят из клеток и не имеют собственных рибосом и цитоплазмы.

nucleus.name: Nucleus
nucleus.rule: The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle that contains most of the cell's DNA, arranged in chromosomes. Genes in the DNA determine which proteins the cell makes, so the nucleus controls the cell's activities. Nuclear pores in the nuclear envelope let copies of genes (mRNA) and other selected molecules pass into the cytoplasm.
nucleus.tip: Mature mammalian red cells lose their nucleus; skeletal muscle fibres commonly contain many nuclei.

cytoplasm.name: Cytoplasm
cytoplasm.rule: The cytoplasm is the cell contents inside the cell membrane, excluding the nucleus in eukaryotic cells. Many chemical reactions take place there and are catalysed by enzymes.
cytoplasm.tip: Glycolysis, the first stage of respiration, takes place in the cytosol, not inside mitochondria.

contrast.en: Cytosol is the watery part of the cytoplasm; the cytoplasm also contains the organelles outside the nucleus.
contrast.ru: Цитозоль — водная часть цитоплазмы; цитоплазма, помимо цитозоля, включает органоиды вне ядра.

membrane.name: Cell membrane
membrane.rule: The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it. It separates the cell from its surroundings and controls which substances enter and leave. The middle of the bilayer is non-polar, so charged and polar particles cannot pass through it easily.
examples: O₂ and CO₂ pass freely (small, non-polar).
Glucose needs a transporter protein.
Ions (Na⁺, K⁺) need protein channels.

mitochondria.name: Mitochondria
mitochondria.rule: Mitochondria are organelles where most stages of aerobic respiration take place in eukaryotic cells. The overall equation is glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Energy released when glucose is oxidised is used on their inner membrane to make ATP. ATP then supplies energy for movement, growth and other processes.
mitochondria.tip: A muscle cell uses a lot of energy when it contracts, so it contains many mitochondria.

contrast.en: Mitochondria release energy from glucose in aerobic respiration; chloroplasts use light energy to build glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
contrast.ru: Митохондрии высвобождают энергию из глюкозы при аэробном дыхании; хлоропласты используют энергию света, чтобы синтезировать глюкозу из углекислого газа и воды.

ribosome.name: Ribosomes
ribosome.rule: Ribosomes are small structures made of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and protein. They read the codons in mRNA and join amino acids in the order specified by those codons to make a protein. Ribosomes have no membrane and occur in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
ribosome.tip: A pancreas cell that makes large amounts of digestive enzymes contains many ribosomes.

contrast.en: The nucleus stores DNA and copies it into mRNA; ribosomes read the mRNA and build the protein.
contrast.ru: Ядро хранит ДНК и переписывает её в мРНК; рибосома читает мРНК и собирает белок.

wall.name: Cell wall
wall.rule: A cell wall is a rigid layer outside the cell membrane. Its material depends on the organism: cellulose in plants, chitin in fungi and peptidoglycan in most bacteria. The wall resists swelling, so the cell does not burst when water enters by osmosis.
wall.watchOut: The cell wall does not control what enters the cell; the cell membrane is the selective barrier.

chloroplast.name: Chloroplast
chloroplast.rule: A chloroplast is an organelle of photosynthetic plant and algal cells. Chlorophyll in thylakoid membranes absorbs light. Thylakoids are flattened sacs, often stacked into grana. Light-dependent reactions use water, release oxygen and produce ATP and reduced NADP (NADPH). ATP transfers energy and NADPH supplies electrons for enzyme-controlled reactions in the stroma, the fluid inside the chloroplast. Those reactions use carbon dioxide to make carbohydrates; sugars such as glucose are assembled from their products. The overall photosynthesis equation summarises many reactions, not a single step in the stroma.
chloroplast.tip: Chloroplasts are common in green parts such as leaves. Ordinary underground root cells generally lack them.

contrast.en: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light; the chloroplast is the organelle that contains it.
contrast.ru: Хлорофилл — зелёный пигмент, который поглощает свет; хлоропласт — органоид, в котором он находится.

vacuole.name: Central vacuole in a plant cell
vacuole.rule: A plant cell's large central vacuole is a membrane-bound compartment containing cell sap. It stores substances and helps maintain turgor: water entry makes the cell contents press against the wall. Vacuoles also occur in other eukaryotes.
vacuole.tip: Loss of water can reduce turgor and cause wilting; a cell wall can remain intact even when its contents shrink.

contrast.en: Cell sap is the liquid inside the vacuole; the cytosol lies outside the vacuole, in the cytoplasm.
contrast.ru: Клеточный сок — жидкость внутри вакуоли; цитозоль лежит вне вакуоли, в цитоплазме.

animalVsPlant.shared: Typical plant and animal cells share a membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria and ribosomes; specialised cells may differ.
animalVsPlant.plantOnly: Typical plant cells have a cellulose cell wall and one large central vacuole. Photosynthetic plant cells also contain chloroplasts.

redBlood.name: Red blood cell (erythrocyte)
redBlood.rule: A red blood cell carries oxygen from the lungs to the body's tissues. Haemoglobin inside it binds oxygen where the oxygen level is high, in the lungs, and releases it where the level is low, in respiring tissues. The cell's shape and contents are adapted to this job.
examples: BICONCAVE shape: thin, with a large surface area relative to volume, so O₂ diffuses in and out quickly.
NO NUCLEUS: more room for haemoglobin (~270 million per cell).
FLEXIBLE: can squeeze through narrow capillaries.
redBlood.tip: Lifespan is about 120 days. Old cells are broken down in the spleen and liver, and their parts are recycled.

contrast.en: Red blood cells carry oxygen; white blood cells (leucocytes) defend the body against pathogens such as bacteria and viruses.
contrast.ru: Эритроциты переносят кислород, а лейкоциты защищают организм от возбудителей болезней, таких как бактерии и вирусы.

neurone.name: Neurone (nerve cell)
neurone.rule: A neurone is a nerve cell that carries electrical impulses. An impulse travels along the cell's membrane; at a synapse, the signal usually passes to the next cell by a chemical messenger. Neurones link sense organs with the central nervous system and with muscles or glands.
examples: LONG AXON: can be over 1 metre (from spinal cord to foot).
DENDRITES: branched ends receive signals from many other neurones.
MYELIN SHEATH: insulates the axon → impulses travel up to 100 m/s.
neurone.tip: Three types: sensory neurones carry impulses in from receptors to the CNS, motor neurones carry them from the CNS to muscles or glands, and relay neurones work inside the CNS.

contrast.en: A nerve is a bundle of axons from many neurones, held together by connective tissue. A single neurone is one cell.
contrast.ru: Нерв — пучок аксонов многих нейронов, скреплённых соединительной тканью. Один нейрон — это одна клетка.

sperm.name: Sperm cell (male gamete)
sperm.rule: A sperm cell is a male gamete, a sex cell that fuses with an egg cell at fertilisation. Its structure is adapted to reach the egg and enter it.
examples: TAIL (flagellum): beats like a whip to push the cell through fluid.
MANY MITOCHONDRIA in the mid-piece: aerobic respiration releases energy as ATP to power the tail.
ACROSOME at the head: releases enzymes that digest a path through the egg's outer layers.
HAPLOID nucleus: 23 chromosomes, half the 46 found in body cells.
sperm.tip: Millions are released at a time, but only one usually fertilises the egg.

contrast.en: A sperm cell is tiny and swims, whereas an egg cell does not swim by itself.
contrast.ru: Сперматозоид мелкий и плывёт сам, а яйцеклетка сама не плавает.

egg.name: Egg cell (ovum, female gamete)
egg.rule: An egg cell (ovum) is the female gamete. It is one of the largest human cells. Its cytoplasm holds stored nutrients for early development after fertilisation; in humans this store is small, and the embryo later gets its food from the mother.
examples: 23 + 23 = 46: the egg's 23 chromosomes join the sperm's 23 at fertilisation.
ZONA PELLUCIDA: a glycoprotein layer around a mammalian egg that the sperm must pass through.
egg.tip: At ovulation, an egg cell is released from an ovary and enters the oviduct. If it is not fertilised, it breaks down.

contrast.en: A zygote is not an egg cell. It forms when an egg and a sperm fuse, and it is the first cell of the new organism.
contrast.ru: Зигота — не яйцеклетка. Она образуется при слиянии яйцеклетки и сперматозоида и становится первой клеткой нового организма.

root.name: Root hair cell (plant)
root.rule: A root hair cell is a cell on the root's outer surface, with a long projection that grows into the soil. Water enters by osmosis, because the cell's contents have a lower water potential than the soil water. Mineral ions usually enter by active transport, moving from a lower to a higher concentration and using energy from respiration.
examples: The projection increases surface area in contact with soil water.
A typical root hair cell grows underground, where there is no light for photosynthesis, so it has no chloroplasts.
root.tip: Found in the 'zone of root hairs' just behind the growing root tip.

palisade.name: Palisade mesophyll cell (plant)
palisade.rule: A palisade mesophyll cell is a photosynthetic cell in the mesophyll, the inner tissue of a leaf. Most of the leaf's photosynthesis takes place in this layer.
examples: PACKED with CHLOROPLASTS: more chloroplasts means more light absorbed for photosynthesis.
COLUMN shape: packed tightly side by side, so the layer catches as much of the sunlight as possible.
Located JUST BELOW the upper leaf surface: closest to incoming sunlight.
palisade.tip: Below the palisade layer lies the SPONGY MESOPHYLL: its cells are loosely packed, with air spaces for gas exchange.

contrast.en: The upper epidermis is a transparent protective layer. Most epidermal cells lack chloroplasts; guard cells are an exception. Light passes through to the palisade layer below.
contrast.ru: Верхняя кожица — прозрачный защитный слой. Большинство её клеток не содержит хлоропластов; исключение — замыкающие клетки устьиц. Свет проходит к столбчатой ткани ниже.

transport.title: Movement across membranes
transport.diffusion: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration due to random motion. It is passive and does not require ATP.
transport.osmosis: Osmosis — diffusion of water across a partially permeable membrane.
transport.activeTransport: Active transport — moving a substance from lower to higher concentration. It is powered by ATP from respiration.

diffusion.name: Diffusion
diffusion.rule: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration, caused by their random motion. Particles move in both directions, but more particles leave the more concentrated region. At equilibrium particles keep moving, but there is no net movement.
examples: O₂ moves from alveoli (high) into blood (low) by diffusion.
CO₂ moves from blood into alveoli (high → low) by diffusion.
Perfume spreads through a room by diffusion, but air currents also carry it, so the spreading is not diffusion alone.
Carbon dioxide enters a leaf through the stomata by diffusion, because photosynthesis uses it up inside the leaf.
diffusion.tip: Surface area to volume ratio (SA:V) falls as a cell or organism gets bigger. Volume grows faster than surface area, so large organisms need exchange surfaces such as villi and alveoli.

contrast.en: Diffusion moves any particles, such as gases or dissolved sugar, from high to low concentration, with or without a membrane.
contrast.ru: Диффузия переносит любые частицы, например газы или растворённый сахар, из области высокой концентрации в низкую, с мембраной или без неё.

osmosis.name: Osmosis
osmosis.rule: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules across a partially permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential. At equal pressure and temperature, dissolving a solute lowers water potential; in the usual dilute-solution model, water moves from the more dilute solution to the more concentrated one.
examples: A red blood cell in a hypotonic solution takes in water by osmosis, swells and may burst.
A plant cell in pure water takes in water and becomes turgid (firm). Its cell wall stops it from bursting.
osmosis.tip: Say which concentration you mean. Compare water potentials: the concentration shortcut assumes equal pressure and temperature. Increased pressure can raise water potential.

contrast.en: Osmosis describes the net movement of water, not solute. In the sucrose-tubing model, the membrane admits water but prevents sucrose crossing.
contrast.ru: Осмос описывает суммарный перенос воды, а не растворённого вещества. В модели с раствором сахарозы мембрана пропускает воду, но не сахарозу.

activeTransport.name: Active transport
activeTransport.rule: Active transport moves a substance across a membrane against the concentration difference, from low to high concentration. The cell uses ATP from respiration for this, and carrier proteins in the membrane move the substance.
examples: Root hair cells take up mineral ions from the soil, even when the ions are more concentrated inside the cell.
Glucose is absorbed from the small intestine into the blood, even when the blood already has a higher glucose concentration.
activeTransport.watchOut: Without oxygen, cells make less ATP, so active transport slows down or stops. Diffusion needs no ATP, so it carries on.

contrast.en: Active transport works against diffusion, using ATP to move substances into a region of higher concentration.
contrast.ru: Активный транспорт идёт против диффузии: он тратит АТФ и переносит вещества в область более высокой концентрации.

significance.name: Significance of diffusion in biology
significance.rule: Diffusion is efficient only over short distances, so exchange surfaces must be thin. Large multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces and ways to transport substances over longer distances. In humans, ventilation and circulation maintain gas-exchange gradients.
examples: The wall of an alveolus is only one cell thick, so oxygen diffuses quickly from the air into the blood.
Insect tracheae carry air close to tissues; many insects also ventilate their tracheal systems.
significance.tip: A good gas exchange surface has a large surface area, thin walls, a steep concentration difference, a moist surface and good ventilation or circulation. Name these features in any gas-exchange answer.

contrast.en: Single-celled organisms exchange gases by diffusion through the cell surface. Large multicellular organisms need specialised exchange surfaces, such as lungs, gills or leaves.
contrast.ru: Одноклеточные организмы обмениваются газами диффузией через поверхность клетки. Крупным многоклеточным организмам нужны специализированные поверхности обмена, например лёгкие, жабры или листья.

osmosisPractical.name: Practical: osmosis
osmosisPractical.rule:
Identical potato cylinders are put into sucrose solutions of different concentrations, each for the same time (for example 30 minutes). The sucrose concentration is the independent variable. The change in mass (or length) of each cylinder is the dependent variable.

When the external solution has higher water potential than the tissue, water enters by osmosis and the cylinder can gain mass. A lower external water potential causes net water loss and can reduce its mass. “Dilute” or “concentrated” must be relative to the tissue under the same temperature and pressure; the concentration label alone does not establish the direction.
examples: In pure water the mass of a cylinder rises from 4.00 g to 4.40 g: % change = (4.40 g − 4.00 g) ÷ 4.00 g × 100 = +10 %. In 1.0 mol/dm³ sucrose the mass falls from 4.00 g to 3.60 g: % change = (3.60 g − 4.00 g) ÷ 4.00 g × 100 = −10 %.

Plot percentage change in mass against sucrose concentration. Where the curve crosses zero change, there is no net gain or loss of water. Use this point to estimate the solution concentration with the same water potential as the potato tissue; it depends on the tissue and conditions.
osmosisPractical.tip: Blot each cylinder dry with a paper towel before you weigh it. Water left on the surface adds mass and hides the real change. Keep the time, the volume of solution and the temperature the same for all cylinders.

contrast.en: Water potential describes the tendency of water to move. Pure water at the reference pressure has water potential zero. At the same pressure and temperature, dissolved solutes lower it; pressure also affects water potential.
contrast.ru: Водный потенциал характеризует способность воды перемещаться. У чистой воды при принятом за отсчёт давлении водный потенциал равен нулю. При одинаковых давлении и температуре растворённые вещества его снижают; давление тоже влияет на водный потенциал.

bodySystems.title: Body Systems
bodySystems.intro: The body's systems work together: nutrition, digestion, circulation, respiration, and the nervous and hormonal systems.

circulatory.title: Circulatory system
circulatory.body: The circulatory system moves blood around the body in a loop. Blood leaves the heart in arteries, passes through capillaries and returns to the heart in veins. Pulmonary circulation links the heart with the lungs, and systemic circulation links it with the rest of the body.

heart.name: The heart — a muscular pump
heart.rule: The heart has four chambers: two atria and two ventricles. The right side pumps blood to the lungs, and the left side pumps it to the rest of the body. Valves open and close as pressure changes, so blood flows mainly in one direction.
examples: Right side: vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs. The blood is deoxygenated.
Left side: pulmonary veins → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → rest of the body. The blood is oxygenated.

The left ventricle has the thickest wall, because it pumps blood around the whole body and needs to generate higher pressure. The right ventricle's wall is thinner, because it pumps blood only to the nearby lungs.
A heart attack happens when a coronary artery is blocked, so part of the heart muscle gets no blood and no oxygen.
heart.tip: Remember the roles: atria receive blood from veins, and ventricles pump it out into arteries. In an exam question, 'receives' points to an atrium, and 'pumps out' points to a ventricle.

contrast.en: A heart chamber is not a vessel. The left ventricle holds oxygenated blood, just like the aorta, but it is part of the heart, not an artery.
contrast.ru: Камера сердца — не сосуд. В левом желудочке, как и в аорте, кровь, богатая кислородом, но левый желудочек — часть сердца, а не артерия.

vessels.name: Blood vessels — arteries, veins, capillaries
vessels.rule: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and veins carry it back to the heart. Capillaries are the tiny vessels where substances pass between the blood and the tissues. Artery walls are thick and contain elastic fibres and muscle, because blood leaves the heart under high pressure. Vein walls are thinner, with less muscle and elastic tissue. Many veins, especially in the legs, have valves that stop blood flowing backwards, but arteries have none, apart from the semilunar valves at the start of the aorta and pulmonary artery. Capillary walls are only one cell thick, and capillaries have no valves.
examples: Feel the pulse at your wrist: the wall of an artery stretches each time the heart pushes blood into it.
In the legs, valves stop blood flowing back down under gravity. When the calf muscles contract, they squeeze the veins and push the blood up towards the heart.
vessels.watchOut: Do not judge vessels by oxygen content: the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs, and the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back to the heart. The names still follow the direction of flow.

contrast.en: The wall thickness and the width of the inner space (lumen) are different things. An artery has a thicker wall, but the vena cava has a much wider lumen than most arteries.
contrast.ru: Толщина стенки и ширина просвета (lumen) — разные вещи. У артерии стенка толще, но полая вена широкая: её просвет больше, чем у большинства артерий.

blood.name: Blood components
blood.rule: Blood consists of plasma, a liquid, and formed elements: cells and cell fragments. Plasma carries dissolved substances, such as glucose, carbon dioxide and hormones. Red blood cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin, and white blood cells help defend the body against pathogens. Platelets are cell fragments that help blood clot. The proportions vary between people and conditions.
examples: Oxygenated blood is bright red. Deoxygenated blood, such as the blood in most of the body's veins, is dark red, not blue; blue is only a convention in diagrams.
A B lymphocyte can develop into a plasma cell, which makes antibodies against a particular pathogen.
A cut: platelets stick to the damaged edge, clotting factors (proteins) form fibrin threads, and the threads trap red blood cells to make a clot.
blood.tip: A red blood cell has a biconcave shape: it is dented on both sides, like a disc. This gives it a large surface area for taking up oxygen.

contrast.en: Plasma is the liquid part of blood. A plasma cell is a different thing: it is a cell, made from a B lymphocyte, that makes antibodies. Both names share the root ‘plasm-’, which is confusing, but they are different concepts.
contrast.ru: Плазма крови — жидкая часть крови. Плазматическая клетка — клетка, которая образуется из В-лимфоцита и вырабатывает антитела. Общий корень «плазм-» сбивает с толку, но это разные понятия.

respiratory.title: Respiratory system
respiratory.body: The respiratory system supplies the blood with oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from it. Two processes make this possible. Ventilation moves air in and out of the lungs and keeps the air in the alveoli fresh. The second process is gas exchange, described below.

pathway.name: Air pathway
pathway.rule: The conducting airways carry air to the alveoli along this route: nose or mouth → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli. On the way, the air is cleaned, moistened and warmed.
examples: The trachea is about 10–12 cm long. Its wall contains 16–20 C-shaped cartilage rings that stop the tube from collapsing. The open side of each ring faces the oesophagus behind it.
Cilia are tiny hair-like structures on the cells lining the airways. They beat upwards and carry mucus, dust and bacteria to the throat, where it is swallowed.
Cigarette smoke damages and paralyses the cilia. Mucus and dust stop moving up and collect in the airways. A strong cough pushes them out: this is the smoker's cough.
Bronchitis inflames the bronchi. In asthma, the bronchioles narrow, so air passes through them with difficulty.
pathway.tip: Remember the size order: from largest to smallest: trachea, bronchus, bronchiole, alveolus. The airways branch like an upside-down tree, and the branches get thinner towards the alveoli.

contrast.en: Air and food both pass through the pharynx. Beyond it, the trachea carries air to the lungs, while the oesophagus carries food to the stomach.
contrast.ru: Через глотку проходят и воздух, и пища, но при глотании дыхательные пути закрываются. Дальше трахея ведёт воздух в лёгкие, а пищевод — пищу в желудок.

alveoli.name: Alveoli — gas exchange surfaces
alveoli.rule:
An alveolus (plural: alveoli) is a tiny air sac at the end of a bronchiole, surrounded by capillaries. The wall of the alveolus and the wall of the capillary are each only one cell thick, so gases travel a very short distance.

Before they diffuse, gases dissolve in the thin moist lining of the alveolus. There are very many alveoli, so their total surface is large and diffusion is fast.
examples: Oxygen diffuses down its concentration gradient. The air in the alveoli has more oxygen than the blood, so oxygen diffuses into the blood. Carbon dioxide diffuses the other way: the blood has more of it than the air, so it diffuses into the alveoli.

Smoking destroys alveolar walls, which causes emphysema, a lung disease. Fewer alveoli means less surface for gas exchange, so less oxygen passes into the blood, even when a person breathes as usual. Smoking is a major risk factor for lung disease and lung cancer.
alveoli.watchOut: Carbon monoxide (CO) from cigarette smoke crosses the alveolar walls into the blood. It binds to haemoglobin much more strongly than oxygen does, so it competes with oxygen for the binding sites. Oxygen transport falls even when the alveoli are undamaged.

contrast.en: One alveolus is tiny, about 0.2 mm across. The large area of about 70 m² is the sum of the surfaces of all the alveoli, not of one.
contrast.ru: Одна альвеола очень мала: около 0,2 мм в диаметре. Большую площадь (около 70 м²) даёт сумма поверхностей всех альвеол, а не одной.

breathing.name: Breathing mechanism
breathing.rule: Air moves into and out of the lungs because the pressure in the lungs changes relative to atmospheric pressure. Muscles cause this by changing the volume of the chest. During quiet breathing in, the diaphragm and the external intercostal muscles contract, and the chest gets bigger. Quiet breathing out is passive: these muscles relax, and the elastic lungs return to their resting size. Forced breathing out, for example when running, needs the work of other muscles.
examples: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle that separates the chest from the abdomen. When you breathe in, your belly moves slightly outwards as the diaphragm contracts and moves down.
A hiccup is an involuntary spasm of the diaphragm. After each spasm, the vocal cords snap shut, which makes the 'hic' sound.
When you cough, the abdominal muscles contract and push the abdominal organs upwards against the diaphragm. This makes the exhalation strong and rapid.
A resting adult breathes 12–20 times per minute. During hard exercise, the rate can rise above 40 times per minute.
breathing.tip: Remember Boyle's law: for a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature, a bigger volume means a lower pressure. When the chest gets bigger, the lung pressure falls and air rushes in. When it gets smaller, air is pushed out.

contrast.en: The external and internal intercostal muscles work in different phases of breathing. The external ones raise the ribs when you breathe in. The internal ones pull the ribs down when you breathe out forcefully.
contrast.ru: Наружные и внутренние межрёберные мышцы работают в разные фазы дыхания. Наружные поднимают рёбра при вдохе. Внутренние опускают их при усиленном выдохе.

digestive.title: Digestive system
digestive.body: The digestive system breaks food down mechanically and chemically, absorbs useful substances and removes undigested material through the anus. Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine.

pathway.name: Route through the alimentary canal
pathway.rule:
The alimentary canal is a tube from mouth to anus. The order of its parts is: mouth → oesophagus → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.

Waves of muscle contraction, called peristalsis, push the food along it.
examples: The stomach absorbs very little. It mixes food with hydrochloric acid and pepsin, then releases it into the small intestine in small portions.
The large intestine digests very little but absorbs water and ions. Without this, faeces would be liquid.
pathway.tip: Remember that 'small' and 'large' describe the diameter, not the length. The small intestine is narrow but long; the large intestine is wide but short.

contrast.en: the alimentary canal from the digestive system. The liver and pancreas belong to the system: they make digestive secretions and send them into the start of the small intestine through ducts. Food never passes through them, so they are not part of the canal.
contrast.ru: пищеварительный канал и пищеварительную систему. Печень и поджелудочная железа входят в систему: они вырабатывают пищеварительные соки и по протокам подают их в начало тонкой кишки. Но пища через эти органы не проходит, поэтому в канал они не входят.

enzymes.name: Digestive enzymes
enzymes.rule:
Digestive enzymes are biological catalysts. They speed up hydrolysis, the breakdown of large food molecules into smaller products that can be absorbed.

Each enzyme has an active site that fits only one kind of substrate, like a key in a lock. Activity depends on temperature and pH, and the optimum differs from enzyme to enzyme.
examples: Amylase breaks starch down into smaller sugars; pepsin breaks proteins down into peptides. Pepsin works best at a pH of about 2 (in the stomach), while amylase works best at a pH of about 7 (in the mouth and small intestine).
Lipase breaks triglycerides (fats) down into fatty acids and glycerol. Bile is not an enzyme.
enzymes.watchOut: Low temperature slows an enzyme down but does not normally denature it. Excessive heat or an unsuitable pH changes the shape of the active site, so the enzyme is denatured and can no longer fit its substrate.

contrast.en: an enzyme from its substrate or product. Amylase is not used up: after it acts, it stays unchanged and can act again. Starch (the substrate) and water are used up, and sugars (the products) are made.
contrast.ru: фермент с субстратом и продуктом. Амилаза не расходуется: закончив работу, она остаётся неизменной и снова катализирует реакцию. Расходуются крахмал (субстрат) и вода, а образуются сахара (продукты).

absorption.name: Absorption in the small intestine
absorption.rule: Absorption is the transfer of digested nutrients across the intestinal epithelium into the blood or lymph. The small intestine, including its last part, the ileum, is adapted for this. Villi (singular: villus) are finger-like projections of the mucosa, the inner lining of the gut. Microvilli are tiny projections on the surface of each epithelial cell. Each villus contains a lacteal, a lymph capillary that takes up fat.
examples: Glucose, amino acids and water-soluble vitamins pass into the blood capillaries of the villi, then reach the liver through the hepatic portal vein.

Most long-chain dietary fats are rebuilt into triglycerides in intestinal cells and packaged into particles that enter lacteals, then lymph and blood near the heart. Glycerol and shorter-chain fatty acids can enter portal blood and travel directly to the liver.
Iron is absorbed in the upper small intestine. Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the ileum, but only with intrinsic factor, a protein made by the lining of the stomach.
In coeliac disease, the immune system reacts to gluten and damages the villi. Absorption falls, so a person can lack nutrients even though they eat normally.
absorption.tip: Why is the surface so large? Over a bigger area, more substance crosses in the same time. The wall of each villus is a thin, single-layer epithelium, so in a villus a substance crosses only one cell layer (the epithelium). The capillary wall it reaches next is also one cell thick. A dense network of capillaries carries absorbed nutrients away, which keeps the concentration gradient steep and diffusion fast. Villi, microvilli and a length of about 6–7 m together give a very large absorption area.

contrast.en: digestion from absorption. Digestion makes molecules smaller; absorption only moves them across the wall. Starch cannot be absorbed until it is broken down into simple sugars.
contrast.ru: пищеварение и всасывание. Пищеварение уменьшает размер молекул, а всасывание только переносит их через стенку кишки. Крахмал нельзя всосать, пока он не распался до простых сахаров.

contrast.en: egestion from excretion. Egestion removes undigested food. That food never passed through the gut wall, so it was never inside the body. Excretion removes metabolic waste made by cells, such as urea (removed by the kidneys) and carbon dioxide (removed by the lungs).

При выделении удаляются продукты обмена веществ, которые образовались в клетках, например мочевина (её выделяют почки) и углекислый газ (его выделяют лёгкие).

nervous.title: Nervous system
nervous.body: The nervous system detects stimuli, processes information and coordinates responses using neurones and supporting cells. The central nervous system comprises the brain and spinal cord; the peripheral nervous system links it with receptors, muscles, glands and other tissues.

structure.name: CNS vs PNS
structure.rule: The CNS consists of the brain and spinal cord. The PNS includes the nerves and ganglia outside the CNS. The optic nerve is an exception: it develops from the brain and is part of the CNS. Sensory neurones carry information to the CNS; motor neurones carry commands to effectors (muscles and glands). Motor pathways are somatic (to skeletal muscles, in voluntary movements and reflexes) or autonomic (to internal organs, generally without conscious control).
examples: A pin prick in the foot sends a signal along sensory nerves (PNS) into the spinal cord (CNS). The response goes along motor nerves (PNS) to the leg muscles.
When you run, autonomic pathways speed up your heartbeat.
structure.tip: The spinal cord is part of the CNS even though it lies inside the spine. The nerves that run from the spinal cord to the arms and legs are part of the PNS.

contrast.en: A nerve is a bundle of many axons in a shared sheath. Most nerves belong to the PNS. A neurone is a single cell.
contrast.ru: Нерв — пучок аксонов (axons) многих нейронов в общей оболочке. Большинство нервов относится к ПНС. Нейрон — одна клетка.

neurone.name: Neurone structure
neurone.rule:
A neurone is a nerve cell that carries signals. Its main parts are the dendrites, which receive signals and carry them towards the cell body; the cell body, which contains the nucleus; and the axon, which carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.

Some axons are wrapped in myelin, a fatty sheath formed by supporting cells. The gaps between sections of myelin are the nodes of Ranvier. A signal passes from one neurone to the next across a synapse; most synapses use neurotransmitters, which are chemical messengers.
examples: The longest neurone in the human body has an axon that runs from the base of the spinal cord to the big toe: about 1 m.
White matter contains many myelinated axons; grey matter contains many neuronal cell bodies, dendrites and synapses.
In multiple sclerosis, the immune system attacks the myelin, so nerve impulses slow down or are blocked.
The fastest myelinated axons conduct nerve impulses at up to 120 m/s; unmyelinated axons conduct them at only about 1 m/s.
neurone.tip: Along a myelinated axon the impulse does not travel continuously. It jumps from one node of Ranvier to the next, which makes conduction faster.

contrast.en: A dendrite and an axon are two parts of one neurone, not two different cells.
contrast.ru: Дендриты и аксон — две части одного нейрона, а не два разных нейрона.

reflex.name: Reflex arc
reflex.rule:
A reflex arc is the pathway that gives an automatic response to a stimulus.

Most reflex arcs follow this order: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone (interneurone) in the CNS → motor neurone → effector (a muscle or a gland). Some arcs have no relay neurone.

Impulses pass from one neurone to the next across synapses. The response is fast because the pathway is short and does not involve conscious thought.
examples: The knee-jerk reflex is the simplest arc: the sensory neurone makes a synapse directly with the motor neurone in the spinal cord, with no relay neurone.
If you touch a hot pan, your hand moves away before you feel the pain. The signal for the response passes through a relay neurone in the spinal cord, not the brain.
reflex.watchOut: Some reflexes are completed in the brainstem. For example, the pupil narrows in bright light, and this reflex runs through the midbrain. Automatic does not mean the brain is not involved: the brain also receives the information, so you may notice the stimulus only after the response has started.

contrast.en: A reflex does not require a conscious decision to start it, unlike a voluntary movement. Many reflexes activate muscles, but some act on glands.
contrast.ru: Для запуска рефлекса не требуется сознательное решение, в отличие от произвольного движения. Эффекторами рефлексов могут быть мышцы или железы.

nutrition.title: Nutrition & balanced diet
nutrition.body: Nutrition supplies the matter and energy needed for maintenance, growth and activity. A **balanced diet** provides enough energy, all essential nutrients, fibre and water, in suitable amounts and proportions. Requirements vary with age, body size, activity and health.

groups.name: The seven nutrient categories
groups.rule: Carbohydrates and fats supply energy; phospholipids, a type of lipid, form cell membranes. Proteins supply amino acids for making the body's own proteins. Vitamins and minerals are needed in small amounts for specific functions. Fibre keeps the gut working well, and water acts as a solvent and transport medium. These are nutrient categories, not seven separate groups of food: one food usually contains several of them.
examples: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy: the gums bleed and wounds heal slowly. Iron deficiency is a common cause of anaemia: less haemoglobin is made, so the blood carries less oxygen.

Three minerals and their roles: calcium builds bones and teeth and helps muscles contract (found in milk, cheese and leafy green vegetables); iron is part of haemoglobin (found in red meat, liver, beans and lentils); iodine is needed to make thyroid hormones (found in iodised salt and seafood).
groups.tip: Nutrient adequacy matters; omitting one named food does not automatically cause deficiency if nutrients come from other sources.

contrast.en: An essential nutrient is one the body cannot make in sufficient amounts, so it must come from food. 'Essential' does not mean 'most important': glucose is vital for cells, but the body makes it, so it is not an essential nutrient.
contrast.ru: Незаменимое вещество — то, которое организм не может синтезировать в достаточном количестве, поэтому его нужно получать с пищей. «Незаменимое» не значит «самое важное»: глюкоза нужна клеткам, но организм синтезирует её сам, поэтому её не относят к незаменимым веществам.

energy.name: Energy requirements
energy.rule: Energy requirement is the energy from food that a person needs each day for metabolism, physical activity and growth. It is commonly expressed in kilojoules (kJ) or kilocalories (kcal), where 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ.
examples: Two people of the same age may have different needs because body size and activity differ.

Calorimetry measures the energy stored in food. A food sample is burned under a tube of water. The energy released heats the water, so the temperature rise shows how much energy was transferred:

E = m × c × ΔT

where E is the energy transferred (J), m is the mass of water (kg), c is the specific heat capacity of water, 4200 J/(kg °C), and ΔT is the temperature rise (°C).

In one test, a 1.0 g sample of peanut heats 0.050 kg of water from 20 °C to 40 °C. E = 0.050 kg × 4200 J/(kg °C) × 20 °C = 4200 J = 4.2 kJ. The same mass of food and the same mass of water must be used in every test, so that foods can be compared.
energy.tip: Metabolisable energy is about 17 kJ/g for carbohydrate and protein, and about 38 kJ/g for fat; values depend on composition. A school calorimetry experiment gives a lower value, because heat escapes to the air and the tube.

contrast.en: Basal metabolic rate is the energy used at rest, measured after fasting. It is only part of the energy requirement: activity and growth add to it.
contrast.ru: Основной обмен (basal metabolic rate) — энергия, которую организм тратит в покое натощак. Он входит в потребность в энергии, но не равен ей: физическая активность и рост добавляют свои затраты.

deficiency.name: Malnutrition — overnutrition and undernutrition
deficiency.rule: Malnutrition is a deficiency, excess or imbalance in energy or nutrient intake. It includes undernutrition, deficiencies of micronutrients (vitamins and minerals), overweight and obesity. A person can take in too much energy and still lack particular nutrients.
examples: A person may eat enough energy but get too little iodine. The thyroid gland then cannot make enough hormone and grows larger, which is a goitre.
A child whose growth is slow may be undernourished, so doctors check growth, nutrient levels and the clinical picture together.
deficiency.watchOut: Adult body mass index (BMI) thresholds cannot be applied directly to children, and no single measurement describes every aspect of nutritional health.

contrast.en: Malnutrition is not only too little food. More is not always better: excess vitamin A (retinol) builds up in the liver and can be toxic.
contrast.ru: Нарушение питания — не только нехватка еды. Больше не значит лучше: избыток витамина A (ретинол) накапливается в печени и может быть токсичным.

respiration.title: Respiration — aerobic, anaerobic, exercise
respiration.body: **Cellular respiration** releases energy from glucose and other food molecules inside cells. Cells capture part of this energy as ATP, the molecule they use for their work. This section compares aerobic and anaerobic respiration, then looks at what happens in the body during and after exercise.

aerobic.name: Aerobic respiration
aerobic.rule: Aerobic respiration needs oxygen. It breaks glucose down completely, mainly in the mitochondria, into carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is used up in the final step, where it combines with hydrogen. Each glucose molecule yields about 30 ATP, and most of the energy is released as heat. The overall equation is in the formula card on this page.
examples: At rest, the brain uses about a fifth of the body's oxygen to release energy from glucose.
Plants respire day and night. In darkness, photosynthesis stops but respiration continues and releases carbon dioxide. In light, net gas exchange reflects both processes.
aerobic.tip: ATP is not energy itself but a molecule that carries energy to where the cell needs it. A cell holds only a small amount of ATP, so it must keep making more.

contrast.en: Oxygen is not a fuel. Glucose supplies the energy; oxygen is needed to release that energy fully.
contrast.ru: Кислород — не топливо. Энергию даёт глюкоза, а кислород нужен, чтобы энергия высвободилась полностью.

anaerobic.name: Anaerobic respiration
anaerobic.rule: Anaerobic respiration releases energy from glucose without oxygen. Glucose is only partly broken down, in the cytoplasm, so the yield is low: a net 2 ATP per glucose molecule. Animal muscle cells make lactate; yeast makes ethanol and carbon dioxide. Fermentation also recycles NAD⁺, a molecule that glycolysis needs. Without it, glycolysis would stop.
examples: In bread dough, yeast ferments sugar and releases CO₂ bubbles, which make the dough rise.
Lactic acid bacteria ferment sugar in kefir and sauerkraut, and the lactic acid they make gives these foods their sour taste.
anaerobic.watchOut: At body pH, lactic acid exists mainly as lactate. Do not confuse lactate with lactose, the sugar in milk.

contrast.en: Anaerobic does not mean no respiration and no energy. Glycolysis, which gives the energy, happens both with and without oxygen.
contrast.ru: Анаэробное не значит «без дыхания» и «без энергии». Гликолиз, который даёт энергию, идёт и с кислородом, и без него.

exercise.name: The body's response to exercise
exercise.rule: During exercise, working muscles need ATP faster than at rest. The heart pumps more blood each minute, breathing becomes faster and deeper, and blood is redirected to the muscles. Together these changes deliver more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide. Aerobic and anaerobic pathways both supply ATP at the same time; their shares depend on how hard and how long the exercise lasts.
examples: A teenager's pulse is about 70–80 beats per minute at rest and can reach 160–180 during fast running.
A 100 m sprint is powered mainly by anaerobic pathways, while a steady 30-minute run is powered mainly by aerobic respiration.
exercise.tip: Heart rate and breathing take a few minutes to reach a steady level. At the start of exercise, muscles use energy already stored in them until oxygen delivery catches up.

oxygenDebt.name: Oxygen debt and recovery after exercise
oxygenDebt.rule: When exercise is hard, oxygen supply cannot keep up with demand, so anaerobic pathways cover the gap. After exercise, oxygen use stays above the resting level until energy stores are restored and the body returns to normal. This extra oxygen use is often called oxygen debt, or excess post-exercise oxygen consumption. Lactate is oxidised in the heart and muscles, or converted into glucose in the liver.
examples: After hard exercise, the extra oxygen restores the phosphocreatine stores in the muscles and refills the oxygen held by myoglobin.
After a hard 400 m race, blood lactate can take about an hour to fall back to resting levels. A gentle jog speeds this up.
oxygenDebt.tip: Muscle soreness that starts a day or two after exercise is usually linked to tiny injuries in muscle fibres, not to lactate.

contrast.en: The oxygen deficit is the shortfall during exercise. The oxygen debt is the extra oxygen used after exercise. The two happen at different times.

endocrine.title: Endocrine (hormonal) system
endocrine.body: The endocrine system is a set of glands that release hormones into the blood. The blood carries hormones to the whole body. Hormones regulate processes such as metabolism, growth, reproduction and the level of glucose in the blood.

comparison.name: Nervous and endocrine regulation: speed and duration
comparison.rule: Nervous signals are electrical impulses that travel along neurones. At a synapse, a chemical messenger carries the signal to the next cell. Hormones need time to reach their target cells through the blood. The effect therefore builds up more slowly, but it can last longer. These are typical differences, not strict rules.
examples: Reflex (nervous): dust reaches the eye → the eyelid closes in a fraction of a second.
Adrenaline (endocrine): a frightening event → effect throughout the body within a few seconds, lasting a few minutes.
Insulin (endocrine): after a meal, it keeps lowering blood glucose for hours.
Growth hormone (endocrine): the growth it causes builds up over months and years.
comparison.tip: The two systems often work together. Under stress, the brain sends a nerve signal to the adrenal glands, which release adrenaline into the blood. The hormone then spreads through the body.

contrast.en: Nervous signals reach specific cells at synapses; hormones circulate widely, but only cells with matching receptors respond.
contrast.ru: Нервные сигналы передаются определённым клеткам через синапсы. Гормоны разносятся кровью, но реагируют клетки с подходящими рецепторами.

hormones.name: Hormones and their effects
hormones.rule: A hormone is a chemical messenger, made by endocrine glands and carried in the blood. It acts only on target cells that have matching receptors. Very small amounts of a hormone can produce a strong effect.
examples: INSULIN (β cells of the pancreas): lowers blood glucose. It helps cells take in glucose and stores the extra glucose as glycogen in the liver and muscles.
GLUCAGON (α cells of the pancreas): raises blood glucose. The liver breaks down glycogen and releases glucose into the blood.
ADRENALINE (adrenal glands): fight-or-flight response. It speeds up the heart, raises blood glucose and dilates the pupils.
OESTROGEN (ovaries): female secondary sexual characteristics at puberty, and regulation of the menstrual cycle. TESTOSTERONE (testes): male secondary sexual characteristics at puberty, and sex drive.
THYROXINE (thyroid gland): increases the metabolic rate. It contains iodine, so the thyroid gland cannot make it without iodine.
hormones.tip: Most hormones are regulated by negative feedback. Example: blood glucose rises → more insulin is released → glucose falls → less insulin is released. Cells need glucose for respiration, so its level is kept within a narrow range.

contrast.en: Insulin and glucagon have opposite effects: one lowers blood glucose, the other raises it.
contrast.ru: Инсулин и глюкагон действуют противоположно: один снижает глюкозу в крови, другой повышает её.

diabetes.name: Diabetes mellitus: when blood glucose control fails
diabetes.rule: Diabetes mellitus is a long-term condition in which blood glucose stays high, because insulin is missing or does not work properly. In type 1, the immune system destroys the beta cells of the pancreas, so little or no insulin is made. In type 2, the cells respond poorly to insulin (insulin resistance), and over time the pancreas cannot make enough insulin to compensate.
examples: Sam (14) has type 1 diabetes. Without enough insulin, glucose uptake by many muscle and fat cells decreases and blood glucose rises. Sam uses prescribed insulin to manage blood glucose.
diabetes.watchOut: Type 1 diabetes is not caused by eating sugary food: its cause is the immune destruction of beta cells. Obesity and inactivity raise the risk of type 2, but they do not show that a particular person has the disease. Type 1 can also start in adults, and type 2 in young people.
diabetes.tip: In an answer, state what is missing first, then explain why blood glucose stays high.

contrast.en: Type 1 always needs insulin injections. Type 2 is often controlled with diet, exercise and medicines.
contrast.ru: Диабет 1-го типа всегда требует уколов инсулина. Диабет 2-го типа часто контролируют питанием, физической активностью и лекарствами.

photosynthesis.title: Photosynthesis & Biotechnology
photosynthesis.intro: Plants use light energy to make organic substances from carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water. This page covers photosynthesis and how humans use genetic engineering to change organisms.

equation.name: The word and balanced equation
equation.rule: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants and algae use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. The carbon in the glucose comes from carbon dioxide. The oxygen released comes from water, which is split during the light-dependent reactions. The net equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
examples: Carbon dioxide + water → carbohydrate + oxygen, using light energy.
Plants respire in daylight too; net gas exchange depends on both rates.
equation.tip: Memorise the equation in BOTH word and balanced form. Note: water and CO₂ are the inputs — light is energy, not a reactant.

contrast.en: One CO₂ molecule does not make one glucose molecule. Six CO₂ molecules are needed for one glucose molecule, because glucose contains six carbon atoms.
contrast.ru: Из одной молекулы CO₂ не получается одна молекула глюкозы. На одну молекулу глюкозы нужны шесть молекул CO₂, потому что в глюкозе шесть атомов углерода.

detail.en: Light reactions and carbon fixation are coupled.

detail.ru: Углерод включается в органику; кислород происходит из воды.

caption.en: A process map, not a one-step chemical mechanism or a claim that energy becomes matter.
caption.ru: Схема процесса, а не одностадийный механизм и не превращение энергии в вещество.

location.name: Where photosynthesis happens
location.rule: In plants and algae, photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts. In land plants, it is especially active in the mesophyll cells of leaves. The light-dependent reactions happen on thylakoid membranes, and carbon fixation happens in the stroma, the fluid matrix of the chloroplast.
examples: Thylakoid membranes hold chlorophyll and other pigments, grouped into photosystems that absorb light.
Xylem brings water to the leaf; phloem carries away the organic substances made there, mainly sucrose.
location.tip: The thin, flat shape of a leaf is an adaptation. It gives CO₂ a short diffusion distance to the chloroplasts and a large surface area to absorb light.

contrast.en: A leaf is an organ; the reactions take place only in the chloroplasts inside its cells. Leaf anatomy is an adaptation for photosynthesis, not the process itself. Most root cells have no chloroplasts, so they do not photosynthesise.
contrast.ru: Лист — это орган, а реакции идут только в хлоропластах его клеток. Строение листа — адаптация к фотосинтезу, а не сам процесс. Большинство клеток корня не имеет хлоропластов, поэтому они не фотосинтезируют.

factors.name: Limiting factors
factors.rule: A limiting factor is the condition that restricts the rate of photosynthesis: if it increases while the other conditions stay the same, the rate rises. Light acts on the light-dependent reactions, and CO₂ acts on the Calvin cycle. Temperature acts on enzymes: they work faster as the temperature rises up to an optimum, but very high heat denatures them, so they lose their shape. When one factor stops limiting the rate, another factor takes over the limit.
examples: Increasing light at fixed CO₂ and temperature can produce an initial rise followed by a plateau.
Water shortage can close stomata and limit CO₂ entry.
factors.watchOut: An optimum temperature depends on the species and conditions; a single universal value is inappropriate.

contrast.en: Light, CO₂ and temperature can all affect the rate, but only the factor in shortest supply is limiting. In bright light with little CO₂, extra light does not help, because CO₂ is the limit.
contrast.ru: Свет, CO₂ и температура могут влиять на скорость, но лимитирует только тот фактор, которого сейчас не хватает сильнее всего. При ярком свете и малом CO₂ дополнительный свет не поможет: предел задаёт CO₂.

model.en: A limiting factor describes one moment, not the whole day. During the day, the limit changes: low light at dawn or dusk is limiting, but at midday CO₂ or temperature may be the limit.
model.ru: Лимитирующий фактор описывает один момент, а не весь день. В течение дня предел меняется: на рассвете и закате лимитирует слабый свет, а в полдень может лимитировать CO₂ или температура.

uses.name: What plants do with glucose
uses.rule: Photosynthetic carbohydrates supply carbon and energy for growth. Plants use them in respiration, store carbon as starch, build cellulose and make other organic molecules. Protein synthesis also requires mineral nutrients such as nitrogen; glucose alone cannot supply nitrogen atoms.
examples: Potato tubers and wheat grains store starch that the plant can later break down into glucose.
Cellulose in plant cell walls gives strength to wood, cotton and paper.
Soya proteins are built from amino acids. Their carbon skeletons come from photosynthetic sugars. Soya obtains nitrogen from absorbed mineral ions and from nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules.
Sunflower and rapeseed seeds convert sugars into fats, which store a lot of energy in a small mass.
uses.tip: Glucose is a convenient product in the simplified overall equation.

contrast.en: Starch and cellulose are both built from glucose units, but the units are linked differently. Starch is a store that the plant can break down; cellulose is a wall material that most animals cannot digest without microbes.
contrast.ru: Крахмал и целлюлоза построены из остатков глюкозы, но звенья соединены по-разному. Крахмал — запас, который растение может расщепить; целлюлоза — материал стенок, который большинство животных без микроорганизмов не переваривает.

experiments.name: Classic photosynthesis experiments
experiments.rule: Photosynthesis experiments test a stated prediction using a control and measured outcomes. A leaf starch test gives indirect evidence of carbohydrate accumulation; oxygen production can estimate net photosynthetic rate. Respiration and storage can affect results, so neither measure directly counts every photosynthetic reaction.
examples: A destarched leaf, partly covered with foil and left in light, turns blue-black with iodine only where it was exposed.
In a pondweed experiment, counting bubbles per minute ignores that the bubbles differ in size; measuring the volume of collected gas gives a more accurate rate.
experiments.tip: Each of these experiments changes ONE variable and controls the others, which is what Criterion B asks for.

contrast.en: A bubble count is not the same as the photosynthesis rate. Bubbles differ in size, and the oxygen released is a net value because respiration uses some of it.
contrast.ru: Число пузырьков — не то же, что скорость фотосинтеза. Пузырьки бывают разного размера, а выделившийся кислород отражает чистый результат, потому что часть его расходует дыхание.

definition.name: What is genetic engineering?
definition.rule: Genetic engineering is deliberate modification of genetic material using molecular techniques. It can insert, remove or alter DNA sequences, including changes within a species. Transferring a gene between species is one example; selective breeding chooses parents without directly editing their DNA.
examples: Engineered microbes can produce a human insulin protein.
Editing a plant gene without adding another species' DNA is also genetic engineering.
definition.tip: Targeted editing can change more than the intended trait, so check both the DNA sequence and the phenotype.

contrast.en: Biotechnology is broader than genetic engineering; engineering can edit existing DNA without adding a gene from another species.
contrast.ru: Биотехнология шире генной инженерии; инженерное изменение ДНК не обязательно переносит ген другого вида.

techniques.name: Key techniques
techniques.rule: Recombinant-DNA methods join DNA sequences, often using restriction enzymes, ligase and a vector such as a plasmid. Gene-editing systems such as CRISPR direct changes to selected sites. Successful delivery does not guarantee correct expression; the modified cells must be checked.
examples: Restriction enzymes cleave selected DNA sequences; ligase joins DNA backbones.
A guide RNA can direct a CRISPR-associated enzyme to a selected DNA region.
techniques.watchOut: Precision is a goal, not a guarantee: off-target and unintended on-target changes must be assessed.

contrast.en: Restriction enzymes cleave DNA, but they do not join it; ligase does the joining. The two enzymes do opposite jobs, so name the one that fits each step.
contrast.ru: Рестриктазы разрезают ДНК, но не соединяют её: соединяет лигаза. Эти ферменты выполняют противоположные задачи, поэтому для каждого шага назови нужный.

applications.name: Applications — medicine, agriculture, industry
applications.rule: Applications of genetic engineering include producing human insulin in microbes, modifying crop traits and investigating gene function. Some treatments alter patient cells to address disease. Each application needs separate evidence of effectiveness and effects; a useful gene does not guarantee a useful organism.
examples: Recombinant protein production uses modified cells as factories for a chosen protein.
Herbicide-tolerant soya survives a spray that kills the weeds growing among it.
applications.tip: When asked about benefits and risks, split your answer into environmental, social, economic and ethical points. For example, less pesticide is an environmental benefit, while gene flow to wild plants is an environmental risk.

review.englishTerm: Biotechnology uses: medicine, agriculture and industry
review.russianTerm: Применения биотехнологии: медицина, сельское хозяйство и промышленность

contrast.en: An engineered crop may carry a herbicide-resistance trait. Repeated herbicide use can select resistant weeds; resistance genes can also spread through reproduction or gene flow where plants can interbreed.
contrast.ru: Генетически изменённая культура может нести признак устойчивости к гербициду. Многократное применение гербицида способствует отбору устойчивых сорняков; гены устойчивости также могут распространяться при размножении и скрещивании совместимых растений.

ethics.name: Ethical and biological concerns
ethics.rule: Ethical assessment of genetic engineering considers likely benefits, evidence about harms, animal welfare, consent where relevant and fair access. Environmental assessment considers gene flow and effects on ecosystems. Biological risk and value judgements are different questions and both require explicit reasoning.
examples: Pollen from a GM crop can pollinate a wild relative growing nearby, so the risk depends on distance and whether the two species can interbreed.
An unaffordable GM seed price can prevent some farmers from adopting the crop and make access to the technology unequal.
ethics.watchOut: Separate evidence about biological effects from ethical judgements, and give reasons for each one rather than assuming every application has the same outcome.

contrast.en: A modified crop can be biologically safe and still raise ethical questions, such as who controls the seed. Safety evidence does not settle the ethical question.
contrast.ru: ГМ-культура может быть безопасной в биологическом смысле и всё же вызывать этические вопросы, например о том, кто контролирует семена. Данные о безопасности не решают этический вопрос.
