ecology.title: Ecology
ecology.intro: How organisms interact with each other and the environment. Energy flow, nutrient cycles, human impacts.

levels.title: Levels of organisation
levels.body:
An individual is one organism. A **population** is all the individuals of one species in a defined area. A **community** includes the populations of different species that live in the same area. An **ecosystem** includes the community, its non-living environment and the interactions between them. The **biosphere** includes all of Earth's ecosystems.

For example, all the oak trees of one species in a defined wood form a population, while the oaks, birds and fungi in that wood are only some of the populations in its community.

contrast.en: A species is not the same as a population. One species can form several separate populations, and each one contains only part of the species.
contrast.ru: Вид и популяция — не одно и то же. Один вид может образовывать несколько отдельных популяций, и каждая содержит только часть особей вида.

foodChains.title: Food chains and webs
foodChains.body: A **food chain** shows one feeding pathway; a **food web** links many pathways. Arrows point from food to consumer, showing transfer of matter and energy. Only some energy becomes new consumer biomass; the rest is unavailable to the next level or dissipates as heat. **Transfer efficiency** is the share of energy that passes from one step of a food chain to the next; it varies between chains.

contrast.en: Matter is recycled: nutrients from dead material return to the soil or water, and producers take them up again. Energy is not recycled: in most ecosystems it enters as sunlight, and it cannot return to the producers.
contrast.ru: Вещество используется повторно: питательные вещества из остатков организмов возвращаются в почву или воду, и продуценты (producers) снова их усваивают. Энергия не используется повторно: в большинстве экосистем она поступает в виде солнечного света и не возвращается к продуцентам.

detail.ru: Питается кроликом; на каждом уровне энергия рассеивается в виде тепла.

carbonCycle.title: Carbon cycle
carbonCycle.body: The carbon cycle is movement of carbon among organisms, air, water, soil and rocks. Photosynthesis incorporates CO₂ into organic matter; respiration, decomposition and combustion return carbon to the environment. Fossil-fuel combustion moves long-stored carbon into the active cycle. This extra CO₂ traps more heat and drives global warming, the rise in Earth's average temperature (see the chemistry section on the greenhouse effect).

contrast.en: A reservoir stores carbon; a flux moves it between reservoirs. Coal is a carbon reservoir; burning it is a flux into the atmosphere. An arrow on a carbon cycle diagram shows this transfer, not the appearance of new carbon.
contrast.ru: Резервуар (reservoir) накапливает углерод, а поток (flux) переносит его между резервуарами. Уголь — резервуар углерода, а его сжигание — поток в атмосферу. Стрелка на схеме круговорота углерода показывает этот перенос, а не появление нового углерода.

waterCycle.title: Water cycle
waterCycle.body: The water cycle is movement of water among stores such as oceans, air, soil, ice and organisms. Evaporation and transpiration add water vapour to air; condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration redistribute it. Solar energy and gravity drive major transfers.

contrast.en: Water vapour is an invisible gas. Clouds are made of tiny liquid droplets, ice crystals, or both; droplets form by condensation. Ice crystals form when droplets freeze or when vapour turns directly into ice (deposition). Precipitation is water that falls from clouds to the surface, as rain, snow or hail.
contrast.ru: Водяной пар (water vapour) — невидимый газ. Облако состоит из мелких капель воды, которые образуются при конденсации (condensation), из ледяных кристаллов или из тех и других. Ледяные кристаллы образуются, когда капли замерзают или когда водяной пар, минуя жидкую фазу, превращается в лёд (deposition). Осадки (precipitation) — это вода, которая падает из облаков на поверхность: дождь, снег или град.

humanImpact.title: Human impacts
humanImpact.body:
Human activities change ecosystems in several ways:

- Population growth increases demand for land, water, food and energy, so more pressure falls on natural ecosystems.
- Clearing forests for farms and cities destroys habitats, divides what is left into patches and changes runoff.
- Pollution includes chemicals such as pesticides and heavy metals, which harm organisms.
- Excess fertiliser nutrients cause eutrophication (see the eutrophication section).
- Introduced species can harm native species: cane toads, brought to Australia to control beetles, now poison the predators that try to eat them.
- Global warming shifts where species can live and changes the timing of seasonal events.

Conservation aims to maintain or restore biodiversity and ecosystem functions. It uses protected areas, habitat restoration and the reduction of threats such as pollution and introduced species. Its success is assessed with evidence such as population trends, habitat condition and genetic diversity.

contrast.en: Conservation is not only about saving one species. Protecting a single species can be one step, but it does not replace protecting the habitat that species depends on.
contrast.ru: Охрана природы — не только спасение одного вида. Защита одного вида — лишь один из шагов, и она не заменяет охрану местообитания, от которого этот вид зависит.

genetics.title: Genetics & Evolution
genetics.intro: This page explains how genetic information is passed on, why individuals in a population differ, and how populations change over many generations through natural selection.

dna.title: DNA
dna.body:
DNA stores hereditary information as a sequence of four bases: A, T, C and G. In the double helix, A always pairs with T and C always pairs with G.

A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a functional product, usually a protein. Chromosomes contain DNA. For example, most human body cells have 46 chromosomes, while gametes (sex cells) have 23.

contrast.en: DNA is the molecule and a gene is a section of DNA. A chromosome contains DNA associated with proteins and carries many genes. Before replication it contains one DNA molecule; after replication it has two sister chromatids, each with one DNA molecule.
contrast.ru: ДНК — молекула, а ген — участок ДНК. Хромосома содержит ДНК, связанную с белками, и несёт много генов. До репликации в ней одна молекула ДНК; после репликации — две сестринские хроматиды, по молекуле ДНК в каждой.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e — 14.2 DNA Structure and Sequencing
sources.section: 14.2 DNA Structure and Sequencing

mitosis.title: Mitosis
mitosis.body:
Mitosis is nuclear division in which the two identical copies of each duplicated chromosome, called sister chromatids, separate and move to opposite ends of the cell. Each new nucleus therefore gets the same chromosomes as the parent cell.

Cytokinesis then divides the cytoplasm, giving two genetically identical daughter cells for growth, repair or asexual reproduction. For example, a human skin cell with 46 chromosomes divides to make two skin cells, each with 46 chromosomes.

contrast.en: Mitosis divides the nucleus; cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm and makes two separate cells. Without cytokinesis, one cell can end up with two nuclei.
contrast.ru: Митоз делит ядро; цитокинез делит цитоплазму и образует две отдельные клетки. Без цитокинеза одна клетка может оказаться с двумя ядрами.

meiosis.title: Meiosis
meiosis.body:
Meiosis is cell division that makes gametes (sex cells) in animals and spores in many plants and fungi. It consists of two nuclear divisions that follow one round of DNA replication, so the chromosome set is halved, from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).

Homologous chromosomes are a pair with one chromosome from each parent. Each gamete receives one chromosome from each pair, maternal or paternal, chosen at random. Segments of homologous chromosomes can also be exchanged (crossing over). These processes generate genetic variation among gametes, although they do not guarantee that every gamete is unique. Fertilisation then restores the diploid number.

contrast.en: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes; meiosis II separates sister chromatids. DNA is not replicated between the two divisions.
contrast.ru: В мейозе I расходятся гомологичные хромосомы, в мейозе II — сестринские хроматиды. Между делениями ДНК не удваивается.

detail.en: DNA replicates before meiosis I; ploidy stays 2n.
detail.ru: ДНК удваивается до мейоза I; плоидность остаётся 2n.

detail.en: Each cell gets one chromosome from each homologous pair; each chromosome still has two chromatids.
detail.ru: Каждая клетка получает по одной хромосоме из каждой гомологичной пары; каждая хромосома пока состоит из двух хроматид.

label.en: After meiosis II: n, n, n, n
label.ru: После мейоза II: n, n, n, n

detail.en: Each of the four cells ends with one copy of each chromosome in its set.
detail.ru: В каждой из четырёх клеток по одной копии каждой хромосомы из её набора.

caption.en: n denotes the haploid chromosome number. Ploidy describes chromosome sets: DNA replication doubles DNA quantity without changing diploid 2n to tetraploid 4n.
caption.ru: n обозначает гаплоидное число хромосом. Плоидность характеризует число наборов хромосом: удвоение ДНК не превращает диплоидный набор 2n в тетраплоидный 4n.

inheritance.title: Inheritance
inheritance.body:
Inheritance is the transmission of genetic information from parents to offspring. Alleles are different versions of one gene, found at the same place on a chromosome (locus).

An individual with two different alleles, such as Bb, is heterozygous. With complete dominance, Bb shows the dominant phenotype. For example, in pea plants the allele for purple flowers (B) is dominant over the allele for white flowers (b). In a genetic diagram, the parents are P, their offspring are F1 and the next generation is F2.

contrast.en: Genotype is the genetic make-up of an organism; phenotype is an observable characteristic influenced by genotype and environment.
contrast.ru: Генотип — совокупность генов организма; фенотипический признак зависит от генотипа и среды.

model.en: One diploid locus, two alleles, equal gamete probabilities, random fertilisation and complete dominance.
model.ru: Один диплоидный локус, два аллеля, равновероятные гаметы, случайное оплодотворение и полное доминирование.

variation.title: Variation
variation.body:
Variation is the difference in characteristics between individuals of the same species. Its causes are different alleles, the environment, or both together.

For example, two people with similar genes can have different body mass if their diets differ.

sources.name: Sources of variation
sources.rule: Mutations create new DNA sequence variants. Recombination and fertilisation combine existing variants in new ways. Environment also affects phenotype, and a genetic effect can depend on the environment.
examples: Pea plants of the same species can have purple or white flowers because they inherit different alleles for flower colour.
Nutrition can affect height, alongside inherited differences.
sources.tip: Mutation creates new alleles; meiosis and fertilisation create new combinations.

contrast.en: Do not confuse a trait with variation: a trait is a feature of one organism; variation is the difference in that trait between organisms.
contrast.ru: Не путай признак и изменчивость: признак — свойство одной особи, а изменчивость — различия этого признака между особями.

continuous.name: Continuous and discontinuous variation
continuous.rule: Continuous variation can take any value within a range, so the measurements form a continuous spread. Discontinuous variation falls into separate categories, with no values in between.
examples: Continuous variation: height in centimetres. A person's height can be 162.5 cm or 162.6 cm, so the values fill a range with no gaps.
Discontinuous variation: blood group (ABO) is A, B, AB or O. A person cannot be halfway between group A and group B, so each person falls into exactly one category.
continuous.tip: Draw a histogram for continuous data, with the bars touching, because the values have no gaps. Draw a bar chart for categories, with gaps between the bars.

contrast.en: Continuous variation is usually caused by many genes working together, plus the environment. Discontinuous variation is usually caused by one or two genes, with little effect from the environment.
contrast.ru: Непрерывную изменчивость обычно вызывают многие гены, действующие вместе, и среда. Прерывистую обычно вызывают один или два гена, а среда почти не влияет.

evolution.title: Evolution by natural selection
evolution.body: Evolution is the change in heritable characteristics of a population over many generations. The best-known mechanism of evolution is natural selection. Extinction happens when the last living member of a species dies, so the species no longer exists. Extinction does not mean that a species was ‘worse’ than others. The dodo of Mauritius was well adapted to an island with no native predators. After people and introduced animals such as rats arrived, it could not survive and became extinct in the 1600s.

naturalSelection.name: Natural selection — 4 steps
naturalSelection.rule: Natural selection is the process in which individuals with heritable traits that suit their environment survive and reproduce more successfully, so these traits become more common over generations. The variation that selection acts on arises by chance: variants do not appear because an organism needs them.
examples: Suppose 1 in 1,000 bacteria carries a variant that resists an antibiotic. If the antibiotic kills 99 per cent of the other bacteria, about 9 in every 100 survivors carry the variant, up from 1 in 1,000 before treatment. The survivors reproduce, so the variant spreads through the population.

In 19th-century Britain, the dark form of the peppered moth (Biston betularia) became more common in industrial areas, where soot darkened tree trunks and dark moths were harder for birds to see. When air pollution fell, the pale form became more common again.
naturalSelection.tip: Heritable variation → more offspring are born than can survive → survival and reproduction are unequal → variants that suit the environment become more common in later generations. This describes selection, not every mechanism of evolution.

contrast.en: Natural selection acts on inherited differences between individuals. Changes acquired during life, such as muscles built by training, are not passed on to offspring.
contrast.ru: Естественный отбор действует на наследуемые различия между особями. Изменения, приобретённые за жизнь, например мышцы, наращённые тренировками, потомкам не передаются.

speciation.name: Speciation — how new species form
speciation.rule: Speciation produces populations that become reproductively isolated. Under the biological species concept, members of a species can interbreed naturally and produce viable, fertile offspring. This definition works well for many sexually reproducing organisms, but it is hard to apply to fossils, where interbreeding cannot be tested, and to asexual organisms.
examples: Darwin's finches on the Galápagos Islands descend from one ancestral population. Groups that were cut off on different islands diverged, and their beaks became suited to different foods.
Birds from two groups whose males sing different songs may not recognise each other as mates, so they rarely interbreed.
speciation.watchOut: Isolation does not guarantee eventual speciation; species boundaries can be incomplete where hybridisation occurs.

contrast.en: A population can change a great deal over many generations and still be one species. In sexually reproducing organisms, a new species usually appears when reproductive isolation stops the groups from interbreeding.
contrast.ru: Популяция может сильно измениться за много поколений и остаться одним видом. У организмов с половым размножением новый вид обычно появляется, когда репродуктивная изоляция (reproductive isolation) не даёт группам скрещиваться.

evidence.name: Evidence for evolution
evidence.rule: Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of organisms from the past. Most fossils form when a dead organism is quickly buried in sediment; over millions of years the sediment hardens into rock, and minerals can replace the hard parts. Fossils in rock layers make up the fossil record, and older layers usually contain forms that look less like living organisms. Some fossils are transitional forms with features of two groups. Archaeopteryx, about 150 million years old, had feathers like a bird but also teeth and a long bony tail like a reptile. The fossil record is incomplete, because most organisms never fossilise, so it supports change over time but cannot show every step.
examples: Homology means the same underlying structure, inherited from a common ancestor, even when it does a different job. For example, a human arm, a bat wing, a whale flipper and a horse's foreleg all have one upper-arm bone, a forearm, wrist bones and finger or toe bones, arranged in the same way, although they are used for grasping, flying, swimming and running.
Almost 99 per cent of the DNA bases in comparable sections of the human and chimpanzee genomes are the same, which fits a close relationship.
evidence.tip: Use several independent lines of evidence to evaluate an evolutionary explanation.

contrast.en: Similar features do not always show close relatedness. Convergent evolution produces similar features in unrelated groups, for example the streamlined bodies of sharks and dolphins, which evolved separately for fast swimming. Homology, in contrast, shows shared ancestry. It is not the same as homologous chromosomes in meiosis.
contrast.ru: Сходство признаков не всегда означает близкое родство. Конвергентная эволюция (convergent evolution) даёт похожие признаки неродственным группам: например, обтекаемое тело акул и дельфинов сложилось независимо для быстрого плавания. Гомология, наоборот, указывает на общего предка. Не путай её с гомологичными хромосомами в мейозе.

humanEvolution.name: Human evolution
humanEvolution.rule: Human evolution is a history of many lineages: several human species lived at the same time, and Homo sapiens is the only one that survives today. Other lineages, such as Neanderthals, became extinct. Fossil and genetic evidence points to Africa as the place where Homo sapiens first evolved, followed by migrations across the world.
examples: Neanderthals and early Homo sapiens lived in Europe and Western Asia at the same time for thousands of years.
People with ancestry from outside Africa typically carry about 1 to 2 per cent of their DNA from Neanderthals.
humanEvolution.tip: Estimates suggest that humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor that lived about 5 to 7 million years ago.

contrast.en: A relative is not the same as an ancestor. Evolution looks like a branching tree, not a ladder, so living apes are not lower steps on the way to humans.
contrast.ru: Родственник — не то же самое, что предок. Эволюция похожа на ветвистое дерево, а не на лестницу, поэтому современные человекообразные обезьяны — не низшие ступени на пути к человеку.

immune.title: Health & Disease
immune.intro: How the body stays healthy and defends itself. This page covers infectious and non-communicable diseases, pathogens, the body's defences, vaccination and antibiotics.

communicable.name: Communicable (infectious) diseases
communicable.rule:
A communicable disease is caused by a pathogen and can pass from one person to another, directly or indirectly.

The pathogen can travel through direct contact, including contact with bodily fluids, in droplets from coughs and sneezes, through contaminated food or water, or through a vector. A vector is an organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another, such as a mosquito.
examples: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spreads through the air when an infected person coughs.
Influenza (flu) is caused by a virus and spreads in tiny droplets from the coughs and sneezes of infected people.
Malaria is caused by a protist (Plasmodium) and is spread by the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito.
Athlete's foot is caused by a fungus and spreads by contact in damp places, such as showers and changing rooms.
Hepatitis B is a viral infection of the liver that spreads through infected blood and other bodily fluids, for example through shared needles or unprotected sex.
Cholera is caused by a bacterium that spreads through water or food contaminated with faeces.
communicable.tip: When you write about an infection, state the type of pathogen and the transmission route.

contrast.en: Infection means a pathogen has entered the body and is multiplying there. Disease means the infection is causing harm to the body, usually with symptoms. A person can be infected with no symptoms and still pass the pathogen on.
contrast.ru: Инфекция — это попадание патогена в организм и его размножение в нём. Болезнь — это вред, который инфекция наносит организму, обычно с симптомами. Человек может быть инфицирован без симптомов и всё же передать патоген другим людям.

nonCommunicable.name: Non-communicable diseases
nonCommunicable.rule:
A non-communicable disease cannot be passed from one person to another, and it is usually not caused by a pathogen.

Causes include genes, problems with body processes such as insulin production, the environment and behaviour. Many chronic (long-lasting) diseases belong to this group, for example heart disease and some cancers.
examples: Cystic fibrosis is inherited: a faulty gene makes the body produce thick mucus that blocks the airways in the lungs and the ducts of the pancreas.
nonCommunicable.watchOut: Some diseases have mixed causes. Cervical cancer is usually caused by a long-lasting infection with human papillomavirus (HPV), but the cancer itself is not passed from person to person.
nonCommunicable.tip: To explain a non-communicable disease, identify one specific cause and show how it affects the body.

contrast.en: A disease can be inherited and still not be communicable. Inheritance means passing genes from parents to children. Communicability means that a pathogen can pass from one person to another.
contrast.ru: Болезнь может наследоваться и при этом не быть инфекционной. Наследование — это передача генов от родителей к детям. Инфекционность — это способность патогена переходить от одного человека к другому.

lifestyle.name: Lifestyle risk factors
lifestyle.rule:
A risk factor is a behaviour or condition linked to a higher chance of developing a disease. Smoking, a diet high in salt, sugar or fat, physical inactivity and heavy drinking are lifestyle risk factors.

A risk factor works through a chain of events in the body. For example, physical inactivity and a diet high in sugar can lead to obesity. Obesity raises the risk of type 2 diabetes.
examples: Smoking raises the risk of lung cancer and heart disease. Stopping smoking lowers this risk over time.
lifestyle.tip: A risk factor increases the probability of disease; it does not mean that every exposed person will develop it. Distinguish evidence of causation from a correlation.

contrast.en: Risk factors can be modifiable or non-modifiable. Smoking and diet can be changed, but age and family history cannot. Both types still raise the risk of disease.
contrast.ru: Факторы риска бывают изменяемыми (modifiable) и неизменяемыми (non-modifiable). Курение и питание можно изменить, а возраст и наследственность — нельзя. Оба вида всё равно повышают риск болезни.

global.name: Global patterns of disease
global.rule: Global patterns of disease show how common illness and early death are in different parts of the world. They depend on the age structure of the population, the environment, exposure to pathogens and risk factors, sanitation and access to healthcare.
examples: In many wealthy countries, non-communicable diseases cause most deaths. In some poorer regions, infections such as diarrhoea from dirty water still cause many child deaths.
Malaria is found mainly in tropical and subtropical regions, where the warm climate suits the mosquitoes that carry the malaria parasite.
global.tip: When you write about a global pattern, state the region, the year of the data and one cause.

contrast.en: A large number of cases does not mean a high rate. The rate compares cases with the size of the population, so a large country can have many cases and still a low risk for each person.
contrast.ru: Большое число случаев ещё не значит высокую заболеваемость (rate). Заболеваемость сравнивает число случаев с размером населения, поэтому в большой стране случаев может быть много, а риск для каждого человека — низкий.

pathogens.title: Types of pathogen
pathogens.body: A pathogen is an agent, usually a microorganism, that causes disease. Pathogens fall mainly into four groups: bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists. Most microorganisms are harmless or useful, so being a microorganism does not make something a pathogen.

bacteria.name: Bacterial pathogens
bacteria.rule: Bacteria are single-celled prokaryotes: their cells have no nucleus, and their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm. Pathogenic bacteria damage tissues or release toxins. They reproduce by binary fission, splitting in two, so a small number of bacteria can quickly become a large population.
examples: Salmonella is a bacterium spread in contaminated food, such as poultry or eggs. It causes diarrhoea, fever and vomiting.
Gonorrhoea is a bacterial sexually transmitted infection. If it is not treated, it can cause infertility.
Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, a slow-growing bacterium. Treatment with antibiotics takes several months.
Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. It releases a toxin that causes severe diarrhoea and dehydration.
MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) is a bacterium that is resistant to many antibiotics, so its infections are harder to treat.
bacteria.tip: In an exam, explain how an antibiotic works. For example, it can damage the bacterial cell wall or block protein synthesis in bacterial ribosomes.

viruses.name: Viral pathogens
viruses.rule: A virus is a non-cellular agent: a DNA or RNA genome inside a protein coat, sometimes with an outer lipid envelope. It reproduces only inside a host cell, where the cell's machinery makes copies of the virus's genome and coat proteins. New viruses leave the cell, often destroying it.
examples: Influenza (flu): the virus mutates quickly, so the flu vaccine is updated every year.

HIV infects T-helper lymphocytes and weakens the immune system. It is transmitted through infected blood, semen, vaginal fluid and breast milk, for example during unprotected sex. Untreated, it can lead to AIDS.
Measles, mumps and rubella are viral childhood diseases. The MMR vaccine prevents them.

COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, a coronavirus identified in early 2020 after an outbreak of pneumonia in late 2019. It spreads in droplets that an infected person releases when breathing, coughing or talking. It led to a worldwide pandemic from 2020.
Tobacco mosaic virus infects plants. Its pale, mottled patches on the leaves reduce photosynthesis.
viruses.watchOut: Asking for antibiotics for a cold or flu is a common mistake. Unnecessary antibiotic use selects for resistant bacteria, so resistant strains can become more common and treatment may become less effective.

contrast.en: A virus is not a tiny cell. It has no cytoplasm and no ribosomes, so it cannot make proteins until it enters a host cell.
contrast.ru: Вирус — не маленькая клетка. У него нет цитоплазмы и рибосом, поэтому белки он сам не синтезирует, пока не попадёт в клетку-хозяина.

fungi.name: Fungal pathogens
fungi.rule: Fungal pathogens are eukaryotes: their cells have a nucleus. They include single-celled yeasts and filamentous fungi, whose bodies are made of hyphae (thin threads). Fungal cell walls contain chitin, which bacterial cell walls do not.
examples: Athlete's foot is a fungal infection caused by Trichophyton. It gives an itchy, scaly rash between the toes.
Ringworm causes a red, ring-shaped, itchy rash on the skin. It spreads by contact with an infected person, an animal or an object.
Thrush is an overgrowth of the yeast Candida. It can follow a course of antibiotics, which kill the bacteria that normally keep the yeast in check.
Aspergillus is a fungus that can infect the lungs of people with a weak immune system.
Powdery mildew is a fungal disease that coats rose leaves with a white, powdery layer.
fungi.tip: Fungi grow best in warm, damp conditions. If a question asks about prevention, explain that keeping the skin dry lowers the risk.

contrast.en: The English name ringworm is misleading. It is caused by a fungus, not a worm, so anti-worm medicines do not work against it.
contrast.ru: Английское название ringworm («кольцевой червь») вводит в заблуждение. Болезнь вызывает гриб, а не червь, поэтому средства от глистов не помогают.

protists.name: Protist pathogens
protists.rule: Pathogenic protists are single-celled eukaryotes: their cells have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Many are parasites that live in or on a host and harm it.
examples: Toxoplasmosis is caused by the protist Toxoplasma gondii. It spreads through undercooked meat or contact with cat faeces.
Amoebic dysentery is caused by the protist Entamoeba histolytica. It spreads in food or water contaminated with faeces and causes bloody diarrhoea.
protists.watchOut: Antibiotics act on bacterial structures, such as the cell wall. The malaria parasite has no such wall, so malaria is usually treated with antimalarial medicines instead.

contrast.en: The pathogen and its vector are different. In malaria, Plasmodium is the pathogen and the mosquito is only the vector, so the mosquito does not cause the disease.

barriers.title: Transmission barriers and body defence
barriers.body:
Transmission barriers keep pathogens from getting inside the body. They are part of innate immunity. They are non-specific: they are not targeted to one particular antigen, although different barriers act differently on different pathogens.

The main barriers are:

- skin: unbroken skin is a physical barrier, but a cut is an entry point for bacteria
- mucus in the airways: sticky mucus traps dust, bacteria and viruses
- ciliated epithelium: the cells lining the airways have cilia, which beat and move the mucus up to the throat, where it is swallowed
- stomach acid: hydrochloric acid (pH around 2) kills most microbes swallowed with food
- tears: they contain lysozyme, an enzyme that breaks down the cell walls of some bacteria

Example: bacteria in the dust you breathe in stick to the mucus in your windpipe, and the mucus is then swallowed and carried to the stomach.

Body defence summary: external barriers help keep pathogens out. Internal innate defences, such as phagocytosis, act on pathogens that get in. Adaptive responses recognise particular antigens and can produce immune memory.

contrast.en: External barriers are the body's first line of defence and part of innate immunity. Adaptive immunity differs because its response to a particular antigen can become faster after an earlier exposure.
contrast.ru: Внешние барьеры — первая линия защиты, часть врождённого иммунитета. Приобретённый иммунитет отличается тем, что после встречи с определённым антигеном ответ на него может становиться быстрее.

immuneResponse.title: Internal immune defences
immuneResponse.body:
Internal immune defences deal with pathogens that get past the external barriers. They include innate responses such as phagocytosis and adaptive responses involving lymphocytes, antibodies and memory cells.

Phagocytes are white blood cells that engulf pathogens. A phagocyte surrounds a pathogen and takes it inside, where the cell's enzymes digest it.

This process is called phagocytosis. It is non-specific because it is not targeted to one particular antigen; it is not equally effective against every pathogen.

Lymphocytes are white blood cells. In the adaptive response taught here, B- and T-lymphocytes have receptors with particular antigen specificities. Activated B-lymphocytes can develop into plasma cells that secrete antibodies. An antibody fits its antigen like a key fits a lock. T-lymphocytes also take part. T-helper cells signal to B-lymphocytes to start their work, and T-killer cells destroy body cells that a pathogen has infected. Other white blood cells also help: neutrophils are the most common phagocytes in the blood, and monocytes become macrophages in the tissues.

Memory cells are lymphocytes that remain after an immune response. On re-exposure, memory B cells can rapidly divide and form plasma cells that secrete antibodies; memory T cells also help provide a faster specific response. This can prevent or reduce illness.

Example: after chickenpox, memory cells usually stop you catching it again.

contrast.en: An antibody is a protein that the body makes in response to an antigen. Do not confuse the two: the antigen is the marker on the pathogen; the antibody is the body's reaction to it.
contrast.ru: Антитело — белок, который организм вырабатывает в ответ на антиген. Не путай их: антиген — метка на поверхности патогена, а антитело — ответ организма на неё.

vaccination.title: Vaccination
vaccination.body:
Vaccination is designed to stimulate immunity without causing the disease. A vaccine presents weakened or killed pathogens, parts of them, or genetic instructions for producing an antigen. The immune response can produce antibodies and memory cells.

Example: the MMR vaccine contains a weakened measles virus. If the person later meets the real virus, the memory cells respond quickly, and the virus is usually destroyed before it causes illness.

contrast.en: Vaccination is the act of giving a vaccine; immunity is the state of being protected from a disease. Do not confuse them: a vaccine helps prevent illness, but it does not cure one that has already started.
contrast.ru: Вакцинация — это введение вакцины, а иммунитет — состояние защищённости от болезни. Не путай их: вакцина помогает не заболеть, но не лечит уже начавшуюся болезнь.

antibiotics.title: Antibiotics
antibiotics.body:
Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing. Some antibiotics damage the cell wall or stop bacteria building it, so the cell bursts. Others block protein synthesis in bacterial ribosomes, so the bacterium cannot make the proteins it needs.

Human cells have no cell wall, and their ribosomes are different, so antibiotics mainly harm bacteria. For example, penicillin stops bacteria building their cell walls, so it can treat a bacterial infection such as strep throat.

A bacterial population can become resistant to an antibiotic. Some bacteria are already resistant before the drug is used, because of random mutations or gene transfer. The antibiotic does not cause this change: it kills susceptible bacteria, and the resistant survivors reproduce and pass the ability to survive the drug on to their offspring.

Unnecessary or inappropriate antibiotic use selects for resistant bacteria. Follow the prescribed drug, dose and duration; the clinician chooses the duration using evidence for the infection. The trait belongs to the bacteria, not to the patient's body.

Antibiotics do not act on viruses, so they are not used for viral infections, and a doctor decides which drug to take and how long the course lasts.

A new antibiotic goes through drug development before a doctor can prescribe it. First comes pre-clinical testing in the laboratory, on cells and animals.

Clinical trials then test the drug on people in phases. Phase 1 checks safety in a small group, Phase 2 checks effectiveness and side effects in patients, and Phase 3 compares the drug with existing treatments in a large group.

contrast.en: Antibiotics act on bacteria only; they do not work against viruses.
contrast.ru: Антибиотики действуют только на бактерии, против вирусов они не работают.

experiment.title: Inquiring and designing (Criterion B)
experiment.intro: Designing a fair test means deciding what to change, what to measure and what to keep the same before any data are collected.

items.independent: Independent variable: the factor you choose to change on purpose. In a pondweed (Elodea) test, the distance from the lamp is the independent variable.
items.dependent: Dependent variable: the outcome you measure after each change of the independent variable. In the same test, it is the number of oxygen bubbles released per minute.
items.controlled: Controlled variables: the conditions you hold constant during the test, such as the water temperature, the size of the sprig and the volume of water. A controlled variable is a condition of the test, whereas a control group is a comparison group that may receive no treatment, a placebo or an established treatment, depending on the question.

contrast.en: One quantity has only one role in a given experiment. Temperature cannot be both the independent variable and a controlled variable in the same test.
contrast.ru: Одна величина в одном опыте играет только одну роль. Температура не может быть одновременно независимой переменной и контролируемой.

hypothesis.title: Hypothesis
hypothesis.body: A hypothesis is a testable explanation for why a pattern occurs. A prediction is what you expect to observe if the hypothesis holds. In a fair test, state the expected relationship between the independent and dependent variables, and give a biological reason for it. For the pondweed test, predict that moving the lamp closer increases the number of bubbles per minute, because more light supplies more energy for photosynthesis while light is the limiting factor.

contrast.en: A research question asks whether a factor has an effect, and it has no answer yet. A hypothesis is written before the test, so it cannot report what was found. A conclusion states what the data showed and whether they support the hypothesis.
contrast.ru: Исследовательский вопрос (research question) спрашивает, влияет ли фактор на результат, и ответа на него пока нет. Гипотезу записывают до опыта, поэтому в ней нельзя писать то, что уже нашли. Вывод описывает, что показали данные, и отвечает, поддерживают ли они гипотезу.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e — 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method
sources.section: 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method

method.title: Method
method.body: A method is a reproducible description of how the data will be collected. It states the samples, apparatus, quantities, timing, measurements, controls and precautions in enough detail for another student to repeat the test. For example, count the bubbles released by a 10 cm pondweed sprig in 3 minutes at each lamp distance. Use a new sprig for each repeat: repeated counts on one sprig include counting and within-plant variation, but do not estimate variation between plants.

contrast.en: The method lists steps, while the results list measured values with their units. A count of 25 bubbles belongs in the results, not in the method.
contrast.ru: Метод перечисляет шаги, а результаты — измеренные значения с единицами. Число 25 пузырьков относится к результатам, а не к методу.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e — 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method
sources.section: 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method

data.title: Data collection and analysis
data.body: Data analysis turns measured values into results that answer the research question. Calculate a mean for each series of repeats, and show the units of every value. An outlier is a value far from the others: check it for a recording error or a faulty step, and justify whether you keep it. For example, bubble counts of 25, 27, 26 and 41 have a mean of 29.75, but without the outlier 41 the mean is 26.

contrast.en: The mean gives the typical value of a series of repeats. The range, the largest value minus the smallest, shows how far the repeats spread. Report both, because a mean alone hides the spread. For example, plant heights of 14.2 cm, 13.8 cm and 14.5 cm have a mean of 14.2 cm and a range of 0.7 cm.
contrast.ru: Среднее арифметическое показывает типичное значение серии повторов. Размах, то есть разность между наибольшим и наименьшим значением, показывает, насколько повторы разбросаны. Указывай оба значения: одно только среднее скрывает разброс. Например, высота трёх растений 14,2 см, 13,8 см и 14,5 см: среднее арифметическое 14,2 см, размах 0,7 см.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e — 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method
sources.section: 1.1 The Science of Biology: the scientific method

evaluation.title: Evaluation (Criterion C)
evaluation.body: Evaluation judges how strongly the evidence supports the conclusion and identifies limitations. Random error changes unpredictably from one reading to the next, whereas systematic error shifts every reading in the same direction. For example, a balance that always reads 0.5 g too high has a systematic error, while readings that vary by 0.1 g between repeats show random error. Reliability means that results are repeatable, and validity means that the test measures what it is meant to measure. Suggest improvements tied to specific limitations.

contrast.en: Describing a trend means stating the pattern with values and units. Evaluating it means deciding how far the pattern can be trusted, given the spread and the limitations.
contrast.ru: Описать тенденцию — значит назвать закономерность числами и единицами. Оценить её — значит решить, насколько можно доверять этой закономерности с учётом разброса и ограничений.

immuneSystem.def: The immune system is the body’s defence against pathogens. It includes barriers such as skin, phagocytes that engulf pathogens, and lymphocytes. Some lymphocytes produce specific antibodies; others become memory cells. Vaccination prepares immune memory before infection.

contrast.en: Innate defence acts broadly; adaptive immunity recognises particular antigens and can form memory.
contrast.ru: Врождённая защита действует широко; адаптивный иммунитет распознаёт определённые антигены и может формировать память.

cellularRespiration.def: Cellular respiration releases energy from nutrients such as glucose for cell activities. Aerobic respiration uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water. When muscles cannot obtain enough oxygen, glucose can also be broken down to lactate, releasing much less energy.

contrast.en: Ventilation moves air into and out of the lungs; cellular respiration is a set of chemical reactions inside cells.

photosynthesis.def: In plants, photosynthesis uses light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen. Chlorophyll absorbs light. A plant can use the glucose in respiration or store it as starch.

contrast.en: Carbon dioxide and water supply matter; light supplies energy. Plants also respire in both light and darkness.

model.ru: Словесное уравнение объединяет множество реакций в хлоропластах. Свет служит источником энергии, а не веществом, поступающим в растение.

ecosystem.def: An ecosystem includes the organisms in an area and the non-living conditions with which they interact. A pond ecosystem includes plants, animals, microorganisms, water, light and mineral nutrients.

contrast.en: Matter is recycled through ecosystems; energy is transferred and eventually dissipated as heat.
contrast.ru: Вещества участвуют в круговоротах; энергия передаётся и в итоге рассеивается в виде теплоты.

dna.def: DNA is the molecule that stores hereditary information. A gene is a section of DNA; chromosomes contain DNA. For example, an inherited gene can affect which pigment a cell produces.

contrast.en: A gene is part of a DNA molecule; a chromosome contains many genes. They are not three names for the same structure.
contrast.ru: Ген — часть молекулы ДНК, а в одной хромосоме содержится много генов. Это разные уровни организации наследственного материала.

evolution.def: Evolution is a change in inherited characteristics of a population over generations. Natural selection can increase the frequency of useful inherited variants. For example, resistant bacteria can become more common when an antibiotic kills susceptible bacteria.

contrast.en: Individuals develop during life; populations evolve over generations. Natural selection is one mechanism of evolution.
contrast.ru: Особи развиваются в течение жизни; популяции эволюционируют в поколениях. Естественный отбор — один из механизмов эволюции.

mitosis.def: Mitosis divides a nucleus into two nuclei with the same chromosome number. After cell division, the daughter cells are usually genetically identical. Mitosis allows growth and repair, for example replacing damaged skin cells.

contrast.en: Before mitosis, DNA is copied. Mitosis separates the copies between two nuclei; division of the cytoplasm then separates the cells.
contrast.ru: Перед митозом ДНК удваивается. При митозе её копии распределяются между двумя ядрами, а деление цитоплазмы разделяет сами клетки.

meiosis.def: Meiosis involves two nuclear divisions after DNA is copied once. It halves the chromosome number and produces genetically different nuclei. In humans it is part of gamete formation: gametes have 23 chromosomes instead of 46.

contrast.en: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes; meiosis II separates sister chromatids. DNA is not replicated between the two divisions.
contrast.ru: В мейозе I расходятся гомологичные хромосомы, в мейозе II — сестринские хроматиды. Между делениями ДНК не удваивается.

foodWeb.def: A food web is a set of connected food chains. Arrows show the transfer of matter and energy from food to its consumer. If grass is eaten by both rabbits and insects, it connects several chains.

contrast.en: A food chain shows one feeding pathway; a food web shows several connected pathways.
contrast.ru: Пищевая цепь показывает один путь передачи вещества и энергии, а пищевая сеть — несколько связанных путей.

biodiversity.def: Biodiversity is the variety of life: differences within species, the number and variety of species, and the variety of ecosystems. Protecting several habitats can conserve more biodiversity than protecting only one species.

contrast.en: Species richness counts species. It does not show how many individuals of each species are present or how much genetic variation they have.
contrast.ru: Видовое богатство — число видов. Оно не показывает численность каждого вида и генетические различия между его особями.

diffusion.def: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from higher to lower concentration due to their random motion. For example, oxygen diffuses from alveoli into the blood.

osmosis.def: Osmosis is net water movement through a partially permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential. A plant cell in dilute solution can gain water and become firm.

activeTransport.def: Active transport moves substances through a membrane against their concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration, using energy from respiration. Root hair cells can absorb mineral ions from a dilute soil solution this way.

enzyme.def: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up a reaction without being used up overall. Its active site binds a suitable substrate. Amylase, for example, breaks down starch.

homeostasis.def: Homeostasis maintains internal conditions within a suitable range despite changes outside or inside the body. Negative feedback helps regulate body temperature and blood glucose.

transpiration.def: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from a plant, mainly through leaf stomata. Water evaporates from leaf cells, and the vapour diffuses out. This helps draw water up the xylem.

xylem.def: Xylem transports water and dissolved mineral ions from roots towards leaves. Its vessels are formed from dead, hollow cells with lignified walls that also support the plant.

phloem.def: Phloem transports dissolved sugars, mainly sucrose, from where they are produced or released from storage to where they are used or stored. Different tubes can transport sugars in different directions.

antibiotic.def: Antibacterial antibiotics kill susceptible bacteria or inhibit their growth. They target bacterial structures or processes and do not treat viral infections. Resistant bacteria can survive a drug that kills susceptible ones.

vaccination.def: Vaccination exposes the immune system to a safe form of a pathogen’s antigens, or instructions to make an antigen. Memory cells allow a faster response if the pathogen is encountered later.
